  4669                              <1> BADPATHPOP:
  4670 0000DBFF 5E                  <1> 	pop	esi ; * 		; Start of next element
  4671 0000DC00 8A06                <1> 	mov	al, [esi]
  4672 0000DC02 08C0                <1> 	or	al, al	; zero if bad element is last, non-zero if path too long
  4673                              <1> BADPRET_X:
  4674 0000DC04 89FE                <1> 	mov	esi, edi		; Start of bad element
  4675                              <1> BADPRET:
  4676 0000DC06 A0[D9AD0100]        <1> 	mov	al, [SATTRIB]
  4677 0000DC0B A2[D8AD0100]        <1> 	mov	[ATTRIB], al		; Make sure return correct
  4678 0000DC10 F9                  <1> 	stc
  4679 0000DC11 C3                  <1> 	retn
  4680                              <1> 
  4681                              <1> ; --------------------------------------------------------------------
  4682                              <1> 
  4683                              <1> ; 11/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  4684                              <1> 
  4685                              <1> SEARCH:
  4686                              <1> FINDENTRY:
  4687                              <1> 	; 02/06/2025
  4688                              <1> 	; 11/05/2025
  4689                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> FINDENTRY) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4690                              <1> 	;
  4691                              <1> 	; Look for a directory entry
  4692                              <1> 	;	(find file name in disk directory)
  4693                              <1> 	;
  4694                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4695                              <1> 	;	;;;[THISDPB] = Base of drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4696                              <1> 	;	EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4697                              <1> 	;	[SECCLUSPOS] = 0
  4698                              <1> 	;	[DIRSEC] = Starting directory sector number (physical)
  4699                              <1> 	;	[CLUSNUM] = Next cluster of directory
  4700                              <1> 	;	[CLUSFAC] = Sectors per cluster
  4701                              <1> 	;	[NAME1] = Name to look for
  4702                              <1> 	;
  4703                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4704                              <1> 	;	If cf = 1 -> name not found
  4705                              <1> 	;	if cf = 0
  4706                              <1> 	;		Zero set if attributes match
  4707                              <1> 	;			 (always except when creating)
  4708                              <1> 	;	;;;[THISDPB] = Base of drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4709                              <1> 	;	EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4710                              <1> 	;	EBX = Pointer into directory buffer
  4711                              <1> 	;	ESI = Pointer to 1st Cluster field in directory entry
  4712                              <1> 	;	;[CURBUF] has directory record with match (MSDOS)
  4713                              <1> 	;	[CurrentBuffer] has directory sector with match
  4714                              <1> 	;	[NAME1] has file name
  4715                              <1> 	;	[LASTENT] is entry number of the entry
  4716                              <1> 	;
  4717                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
  4718                              <1> 	;	EAX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP
  4719                              <1> 	;
  4720                              <1> 
  4721 0000DC12 E8D9000000          <1> 	call	STARTSRCH
  4722 0000DC17 A0[D8AD0100]        <1> 	mov	al, [ATTRIB]
  4723 0000DC1C 24DE                <1> 	and	al, ~attr_ignore	; Ignore useless bits
  4724 0000DC1E 3C08                <1> 	cmp	al, attr_volume_id	; Looking for vol ID only ?
  4725 0000DC20 7505                <1> 	jne	short NotVolSrch	; No
  4726 0000DC22 E86AFBFFFF          <1> 	call	SETROOTSRCH		; Yes force search of root
  4727                              <1> NotVolSrch:	
  4728 0000DC27 E8DC000000          <1> 	call	GETENTRY
  4729 0000DC2C 7242                <1> 	jc	short SETESRET
  4730                              <1> 
  4731                              <1> 	; EBX = Pointer to next directory entry in CURBUF
  4732                              <1> 	; ECX = Pointer to first byte after end of CURBUF
  4733                              <1> 	; [LASTENT] = New directory entry number
  4734                              <1> 	; [NXTCLUSNUM],[SECCLUSPOS] set
  4735                              <1> 	; EDX = LDRVT address (MSDOS -> [THISDPB])
  4736                              <1> SRCH:
  4737                              <1> 	;mov	word [LNE_COUNT], 0	; reset long name entry count
  4738 0000DC2E C605[F8AD0100]00    <1> 	mov	byte [LNE_COUNT], 0	; reset long name entry count
  4739                              <1> SRCH2:
  4740 0000DC35 8A23                <1> 	mov	ah, [ebx] ; [ebx+dir_entry.dir_name] ; mov ah, [ebx+0]
  4741 0000DC37 08E4                <1> 	or	ah, ah
  4742 0000DC39 745A                <1> 	jz	short findentry_free
  4743 0000DC3B 8A430B              <1> 	mov	al, [ebx+dir_entry.dir_attr] ; [ebx+0Bh]
  4744 0000DC3E 50                  <1> 	push	eax
  4745 0000DC3F E803010000          <1> 	call	check_longname
  4746 0000DC44 58                  <1> 	pop	eax
  4747 0000DC45 743F                <1> 	jz	short NEXTENT2
  4748                              <1> 
  4749 0000DC47 3A25[E8AD0100]      <1> 	cmp	ah, [DELALL]		; Free entry?
  4750 0000DC4D 7446                <1> 	je	short findentry_free
  4751                              <1> 
  4752 0000DC4F F6430B08            <1> 	test	byte [ebx+dir_entry.dir_attr], attr_volume_id
  4753                              <1> 					; Volume ID file?
  4754 0000DC53 7406                <1> 	jz	short CHKFNAM 		; NO
  4755                              <1> 
  4756 0000DC55 FE05[E9AD0100]      <1> 	inc	byte [VOLID]
  4757                              <1> CHKFNAM:
  4758 0000DC5B 89DF                <1> 	mov	edi, ebx  ; no possible '?' ; directory entry
  4759 0000DC5D BE[DAAD0100]        <1> 	mov	esi, NAME1 ; possible '?'
  4760 0000DC62 E81CFAFFFF          <1> 	call	METACOMPARE
  4761 0000DC67 7451                <1> 	jz	short findentry_found
  4762                              <1> NEXTENT:
  4763                              <1> 	;mov	edx, [THISDPB]
  4764                              <1> 	; edx = Logical DOS Drive Description Table address
  4765 0000DC69 E8E6000000          <1> 	call	NEXTENTRY
  4766 0000DC6E 73BE                <1> 	jnc	short SRCH
  4767                              <1> SETESRET:
  4768 0000DC70 FF35[ECAD0100]      <1> 	push	dword [ENTLAST]
  4769 0000DC76 8F05[F4AD0100]      <1> 	pop	dword [ENTLAST_PREV]	; previous ENTLAST
  4770 0000DC7C 7207                <1> 	jc	short SETESRETN
  4771                              <1> 	;mov	word [LNE_COUNT], 0	; reset long name entry count
  4772 0000DC7E C605[F8AD0100]00    <1> 	mov	byte [LNE_COUNT], 0	; reset long name entry count
  4773                              <1> SETESRETN:
  4774 0000DC85 C3                  <1> 	retn
  4775                              <1> 
  4776                              <1> NEXTENT2:
  4777                              <1> 	;inc	word [LNE_COUNT]	; Long Name entry count
  4778 0000DC86 FE05[F8AD0100]      <1> 	inc	byte [LNE_COUNT]
  4779                              <1> NEXTENT3:
  4780                              <1> 	;mov	edx, [THISDPB]
  4781                              <1> 	; edx = Logical DOS Drive Description Table address
  4782 0000DC8C E8C3000000          <1> 	call	NEXTENTRY
  4783 0000DC91 73A2                <1> 	jnc	short SRCH2
  4784 0000DC93 EBDB                <1> 	jmp	short SETESRET
  4785                              <1> 
  4786                              <1> findentry_free:
  4787 0000DC95 8B0D[C8AD0100]      <1> 	mov	ecx, [LASTENT]
  4788 0000DC9B 3B0D[F0AD0100]      <1> 	cmp	ecx, [ENTFREE]
  4789 0000DCA1 7306                <1> 	jae	short TSTALL
  4790 0000DCA3 890D[F0AD0100]      <1> 	mov	[ENTFREE], ecx
  4791                              <1> TSTALL:
  4792 0000DCA9 3A25[E8AD0100]      <1> 	cmp	ah, [DELALL]		; At end of directory?
  4793 0000DCAF 74DB                <1> 	je	short NEXTENT3		; No - continue search
  4794 0000DCB1 890D[ECAD0100]      <1> 	mov	[ENTLAST], ecx
  4795 0000DCB7 F9                  <1> 	stc
  4796 0000DCB8 EBB6                <1> 	jmp	short SETESRET
  4797                              <1> 
  4798                              <1> findentry_found:
  4799                              <1> 	; We have a file with a matching name.
  4800                              <1> 	; We must now consider the attributes:
  4801                              <1> 	
  4802                              <1> 	; ATTRIB     Action
  4803                              <1> 	; ------     ------
  4804                              <1> 	; Volume_ID  Is Volume_ID in test?
  4805                              <1> 	; Otherwise  If no create then Is ATTRIB+extra superset of test?
  4806                              <1> 	;	     If create then Is ATTRIB equal to test?
  4807                              <1> 
  4808 0000DCBA 8A2E                <1> 	mov	ch, [esi]		; Attributes of file
  4809 0000DCBC 8A25[D8AD0100]      <1> 	mov	ah, [ATTRIB]		; Attributes of search
  4810                              <1> 	;and	ah, 9Eh
  4811 0000DCC2 80E4DE              <1> 	and	ah, ~attr_ignore
  4812                              <1> 	;lea	esi, [esi+15]
  4813 0000DCC5 8D760F              <1> 	lea	esi, [esi+dir_entry.dir_first-dir_entry.dir_attr]
  4814                              <1> 					; point to first cluster field
  4815                              <1> 	;test	ch, 8
  4816 0000DCC8 F6C508              <1> 	test	ch, attr_volume_id	; Volume ID file?
  4817 0000DCCB 7409                <1> 	jz	short check_one_volume_id ; Nope check other attributes
  4818                              <1> 	;test	ah, 8
  4819 0000DCCD F6C408              <1> 	test	ah, attr_volume_id	; Can we find Volume ID?
  4820 0000DCD0 7497                <1> 	jz	short NEXTENT 		; Nope
  4821 0000DCD2 30E4                <1> 	xor	ah, ah			; Set zero flag
  4822                              <1> 	; zf = 1
  4823 0000DCD4 EB9A                <1> 	jmp	short SETESRET
  4824                              <1> 
  4825                              <1> check_one_volume_id:
  4826                              <1> 	;cmp	ah, 8
  4827 0000DCD6 80FC08              <1> 	cmp	ah, attr_volume_id	; Looking only for Volume ID?
  4828 0000DCD9 748E                <1> 	je	short NEXTENT		; Yes, continue search
  4829 0000DCDB E85B000000          <1> 	call	MATCHATTRIBUTES
  4830 0000DCE0 748E                <1> 	jz	short SETESRET
  4831 0000DCE2 F605[E7AD0100]FF    <1> 	test	byte [CREATING], -1	; Pass back mismatch if creating
  4832                              <1> 	;jz	short NEXTENT		; Otherwise continue searching
  4833                              <1> 	;; zf = 0
  4834                              <1> 	;jmp	short SETESRET
  4835                              <1> 	; 02/06/2025
  4836 0000DCE9 7585                <1> 	jnz	short SETESRET
  4837                              <1> 	; zf = 1
  4838 0000DCEB E979FFFFFF          <1> 	jmp	NEXTENT
  4839                              <1> 
  4840                              <1> ; --------------------------------------------------------------------
  4841                              <1> 
  4842                              <1> ; 11/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  4843                              <1> 
  4844                              <1> STARTSRCH:
  4845                              <1> 	; 11/05/2025
  4846                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> STARTSRCH) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4847                              <1> 	;
  4848                              <1> 	; Initiate a directory search
  4849                              <1> 	;	(Set up a search for GETENTRY and NEXTENTRY)
  4850                              <1> 	;
  4851                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4852                              <1> 	;	;;;[THISDPB] = Base of drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4853                              <1> 	;	;EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4854                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4855                              <1> 	;	;;;ES:BP = Drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4856                              <1> 	;	;EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4857                              <1> 	;
  4858                              <1> 	;	Sets up LASTENT=VOLID=0, ENTFREE=ENTLAST=-1
  4859                              <1> 	;
  4860                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
  4861                              <1> 	;	EAX
  4862                              <1> 	;
  4863                              <1> 
  4864                              <1> 	;;;;les	bp, [THISDPB]
  4865                              <1> 
  4866 0000DCF0 31C0                <1> 	xor	eax, eax ; 0
  4867 0000DCF2 A3[C8AD0100]        <1> 	mov	[LASTENT], eax
  4868 0000DCF7 A2[E9AD0100]        <1> 	mov	[VOLID], al ; 0	; No volume ID found
  4869 0000DCFC 48                  <1> 	dec	eax ; -1
  4870 0000DCFD A3[F0AD0100]        <1> 	mov	[ENTFREE], eax
  4871 0000DD02 A3[ECAD0100]        <1> 	mov	[ENTLAST], eax
  4872 0000DD07 C3                  <1> 	retn
  4873                              <1> 
  4874                              <1> 
  4875                              <1> ; --------------------------------------------------------------------
  4876                              <1> 
  4877                              <1> ; 11/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  4878                              <1> 
  4879                              <1> GETENTRY:
  4880                              <1> 	; 11/05/2025
  4881                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> GETENTRY) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4882                              <1> 	;
  4883                              <1> 	; Locates directory entry in preparation for search
  4884                              <1> 	; (GETENT provides entry for passing desired entry in EAX)
  4885                              <1> 	;
  4886                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4887                              <1> 	;	[LASTENT] has directory entry
  4888                              <1> 	;	EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4889                              <1> 	;	[DIRSEC],[CLUSNUM],[CLUSFAC],[ENTLAST] set
  4890                              <1> 	;					 for DIR involved
  4891                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4892                              <1> 	;	EBX = Pointer to next directory entry in CURBUF
  4893                              <1> 	;	ECX = Pointer to first byte after end of CURBUF
  4894                              <1> 	;	[LASTENT] = New directory entry number
  4895                              <1> 	;	[NXTCLUSNUM],[SECCLUSPOS] set via DIRREAD
  4896                              <1> 	;
  4897                              <1> 	;	Carry set if error
  4898                              <1> 	;
  4899                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
  4900                              <1> 	;	EAX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP
  4901                              <1> 	;
  4902                              <1> 
  4903                              <1> ;GETENTRY:
  4904 0000DD08 A1[C8AD0100]        <1> 	mov	eax, [LASTENT]
  4905                              <1> 	; 11/05/2025
  4906 0000DD0D EB05                <1> 	jmp	short GETENT_@
  4907                              <1> GETENT:
  4908 0000DD0F A3[C8AD0100]        <1> 	mov	[LASTENT], eax
  4909                              <1> GETENT_@:
  4910                              <1> 	; Convert the entry number in EAX into a byte offset
  4911                              <1> 	;	from the beginning of the directory
  4912 0000DD14 C1E005              <1> 	shl	eax, 5 ; * 32
  4913 0000DD17 89D3                <1> 	mov	ebx, edx
  4914 0000DD19 31D2                <1> 	xor	edx, edx ; 0
  4915                              <1> 	;mov	ecx, 512
  4916 0000DD1B 0FB74B11            <1> 	movzx	ecx, word [ebx+LD_BPB+BytesPerSec]
  4917 0000DD1F F7F1                <1> 	div	ecx
  4918 0000DD21 87DA                <1> 	xchg	ebx, edx
  4919                              <1> 
  4920 0000DD23 51                  <1> 	push	ecx ; bytes per sector	
  4921 0000DD24 53                  <1> 	push	ebx ; byte offset to dir entry
  4922                              <1> 
  4923                              <1> 	; eax = directory block (index) number
  4924                              <1> 	;	(relative to the first block of directory)
  4925                              <1> 	; edx = Logical DOS Drive Description Table address
  4926                              <1> 	; [DIRSEC] = First physical sector of 1st cluster of dir
  4927                              <1> 	; [CLUSNUM] = Next cluster
  4928                              <1> 	; [CLUSFAC] = Sectors/Cluster ; not used
  4929                              <1> 	
  4930 0000DD25 E8CEFAFFFF          <1> 	call	DIRREAD
  4931 0000DD2A 5B                  <1> 	pop	ebx ; byte offset to dir entry
  4932 0000DD2B 59                  <1> 	pop	ecx ; bytes per sector
  4933 0000DD2C 720C                <1> 	jc	short getentry_retn
  4934                              <1> 
  4935                              <1> 	; [NXTCLUSNUM] = Next cluster (after the one skipped to)
  4936                              <1> 	; [SECCLUSPOS] Set
  4937                              <1> 	; [CURBUF] points to Buffer with dir sector
  4938                              <1> 
  4939                              <1> SETENTRY:
  4940 0000DD2E A1[A4AD0100]        <1> 	mov	eax, [CurrentBuffer] ; (MSDOS -> [CURBUF])
  4941 0000DD33 83C018              <1> 	add	eax, BUFINSIZ
  4942 0000DD36 01C3                <1> 	add	ebx, eax
  4943 0000DD38 01C1                <1> 	add	ecx, eax
  4944                              <1> 	;clc
  4945                              <1> getentry_retn:
  4946 0000DD3A C3                  <1> 	retn
  4947                              <1> 
  4948                              <1> ; --------------------------------------------------------------------
  4949                              <1> 
  4950                              <1> ; 12/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  4951                              <1> 
  4952                              <1> MATCHATTRIBUTES:
  4953                              <1> 	; 12/05/2025
  4954                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> MATCHATTRIBUTES) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4955                              <1> 	;
  4956                              <1> 	; the final check for attribute matching
  4957                              <1> 	;
  4958                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4959                              <1> 	;	[ATTRIB] = attribute to search for
  4960                              <1> 	;	CH = found attribute
  4961                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4962                              <1> 	;	JZ <match>
  4963                              <1> 	;	JNZ <nomatch>
  4964                              <1> 	;
  4965                              <1> 	; Modified registers: EAX
  4966                              <1> 	;
  4967                              <1> 
  4968 0000DD3B A0[D8AD0100]        <1> 	mov	al, [ATTRIB]	; searchset
  4969 0000DD40 F6D0                <1> 	not	al		; searchset'
  4970 0000DD42 20E8                <1> 	and	al, ch		; searchset' and foundset
  4971                              <1> 	;and	al, 16h
  4972 0000DD44 2416                <1> 	and	al, attr_all	; searchset' & foundset & important
  4973 0000DD46 C3                  <1> 	retn
  4974                              <1>

  4976                              <1> 
  4977                              <1> ; 12/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  4978                              <1> 
  4979                              <1> check_longname:
  4980                              <1> 	; 12/05/2025
  4981                              <1> 	; (PCDOS 7.1 -> ?) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4982                              <1> 	; ((ref: FAT32 File System Specification)) (Microsoft)
  4983                              <1> 	;
  4984                              <1> 	; check directry entry attribute 
  4985                              <1> 	; if the entry is longname sub component of not
  4986                              <1> 	;
  4987                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4988                              <1> 	;	AL = attribute to search for
  4989                              <1> 	;	AH = first character of DirEntry_Name
  4990                              <1> 	;			(LDIR_Ord)
  4991                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4992                              <1> 	;	JZ <match>
  4993                              <1> 	;	JNZ <nomatch>
  4994                              <1> 	;
  4995                              <1> 	; Modified registers: EAX (AL)
  4996                              <1> 	;
  4997                              <1> 
  4998 0000DD47 80FCE5              <1> 	cmp	ah, 0E5h
  4999 0000DD4A 7503                <1> 	jne	short chk_lname_@
  5000 0000DD4C 20E4                <1> 	and	ah, ah
  5001                              <1> 	; zf = 0
  5002 0000DD4E C3                  <1> 	retn
  5003                              <1> chk_lname_@:
  5004                              <1> 	;and	al, 0Fh
  5005 0000DD4F 243F                <1> 	and	al, ATTR_LONGNAME_MASK ; 3Fh
  5006                              <1> 	;cmp	al, 0Fh
  5007 0000DD51 3C0F                <1> 	cmp	al, ATTR_LONGNAME ; 0Fh
  5008 0000DD53 C3                  <1> 	retn
  5009                              <1>

  5014                              <1> 
  5015                              <1> NEXTENTRY:
  5016 0000DD54 F9                  <1> 	stc
  5017 0000DD55 C3                  <1> 	retn

  5020                              <1> 
  5021                              <1> ; 10/07/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  5022                              <1> 
  5023                              <1> PACK:
  5024                              <1> 	; 03/12/2025
  5025                              <1> 	; 26/11/2025
  5026                              <1> 	; 25/11/2025
  5027                              <1> 	; 22/07/2025
  5028                              <1> 	; 10/07/2025
  5029                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> PACK) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  5030                              <1> 	; Pack FAT entries (ALLOCATE)
  5031                              <1> 	;
  5032                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  5033                              <1> 	;	edx = Logical DOS Drive Description Table address
  5034                              <1> 	;	eax = Cluster Number (28bit for FAT32 fs)
  5035                              <1> 	;	ebx = Data
  5036                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  5037                              <1> 	;	The data is stored in the FAT at the given cluster.
  5038                              <1> 	;
  5039                              <1> 	;	if cf = 1, eax = error code
  5040                              <1> 	;
  5041                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
  5042                              <1> 	;	eax, ecx, ebx, esi, edi, ebp
  5043                              <1> 
  5044 0000DD56 09C0                <1> 	or	eax, eax
  5045 0000DD58 7507                <1> 	jnz	short pack_1
  5046                              <1>

    20                              <1> sysent: ; < enter to system call >
    21                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.1.0
    22                              <1> 	; 01/05/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.11
    23                              <1> 	; 08/01/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10 (v2.1.0)
    24                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
    25                              <1> 	; 17/03/2017
    26                              <1> 	; 03/03/2017
    27                              <1> 	; 19/02/2017
    28                              <1> 	; 13/01/2017
    29                              <1> 	; 06/06/2016
    30                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
    31                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 - 19/10/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
    32                              <1> 	; 10/04/2013 - 18/01/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
    33                              <1> 	;
    34                              <1> 	; 'unkni' or 'sysent' is sytem entry from various traps.
    35                              <1> 	; The trap type is determined and an indirect jump is made to
    36                              <1> 	; the appropriate system call handler. If there is a trap inside
    37                              <1> 	; the system a jump to panic is made. All user registers are saved
    38                              <1> 	; and u.sp points to the end of the users stack. The sys (trap)
    39                              <1> 	; instructor is decoded to get the the system code part (see
    40                              <1> 	; trap instruction in the PDP-11 handbook) and from this
    41                              <1> 	; the indirect jump address is calculated. If a bad system call is
    42                              <1> 	; made, i.e., the limits of the jump table are exceeded, 'badsys'
    43                              <1> 	; is called. If the call is legitimate control passes to the
    44                              <1> 	; appropriate system routine.
    45                              <1> 	;
    46                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
    47                              <1> 	;	Through a trap caused by any sys call outside the system.
    48                              <1> 	; Arguments:
    49                              <1> 	;	Arguments of particular system call.
    50                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
    51                              <1> 	;
    52                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
    53                              <1> 	;       System call number is in EAX register.
    54                              <1> 	;
    55                              <1> 	;       Other parameters are in EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP
    56                              <1> 	;	registers depending of function details.
    57                              <1>   	;
    58                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015
    59 0000DF8A 368925[0CB00100]    <1>         mov     [ss:u.sp], esp ; Kernel stack points to return address
    60                              <1> 
    61                              <1> 	; save user registers
    62 0000DF91 1E                  <1> 	push	ds
    63 0000DF92 06                  <1> 	push	es
    64 0000DF93 0FA0                <1> 	push	fs
    65 0000DF95 0FA8                <1> 	push	gs
    66 0000DF97 60                  <1> 	pushad  ; eax, ecx, edx, ebx, esp -before pushad-, ebp, esi, edi
    67                              <1> 	;

   286                              <1> sysemt: ; enable (or disable) multi tasking -time sharing-
   287                              <1> 	;
   288                              <1> 	; 08/08/2022
   289                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
   290                              <1> 	; 23/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
   291                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
   292                              <1> 	; 10/12/2013 - 20/04/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
   293                              <1> 	;
   294                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
   295                              <1> 	;	'Enable Multi Tasking'  system call instead
   296                              <1> 	;	of 'Emulator Trap' in original UNIX v1 for PDP-11.
   297                              <1> 	;
   298                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 feature only!
   299                              <1> 	;	Using purpose: Kernel will start without time-out
   300                              <1> 	;	(internal clock/timer) functionality.
   301                              <1> 	;	Then etc/init will enable clock/timer for
   302                              <1> 	;	multi tasking.
   303                              <1> 	;
   304                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
   305                              <1> 	;	BL = 0 -> disable multi tasking
   306                              <1> 	;	BL > 1 -> enable multi tasking (time sharing)
   307                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
   308                              <1> 	;	none
   309                              <1> 	;
   310                              <1> 	;  Note: Multi tasking is disabled during system
   311                              <1> 	;	 initialization, it must be enabled by using
   312                              <1> 	;	 this system call. (Otherwise, running proces 
   313                              <1> 	;	 will not be changed by another process within
   314                              <1> 	;	 run time sequence/schedule, if running process
   315                              <1> 	;	 will not 'release' itself. Only 'wakeup' procedure
   316                              <1> 	;	 for waiting processes and programmed timer events
   317                              <1> 	;	 for other processes can change running process
   318                              <1> 	;	 while multi tasking is disabled.) ** 23/05/2016 **
   319                              <1>

   339                              <1> 	; 'error' merely sets the error bit off the processor status (c-bit)

   377                              <1> sysret: ; < return from system call>
   378                              <1> 	; 28/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9
   379                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
   380                              <1> 	; 01/03/2017
   381                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017
   382                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
   383                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 - 10/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
   384                              <1> 	; 10/04/2013 - 23/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
   385                              <1> 	;
   386                              <1> 	; 'sysret' first checks to see if process is about to be
   387                              <1> 	; terminated (u.bsys). If it is, 'sysexit' is called.
   388                              <1> 	; If not, following happens:
   389                              <1> 	; 	1) The user's stack pointer is restored.
   390                              <1> 	;	2) r1=0 and 'iget' is called to see if last mentioned
   391                              <1> 	;	   i-node has been modified. If it has, it is written out
   392                              <1> 	;	   via 'ppoke'.
   393                              <1> 	;	3) If the super block has been modified, it is written out
   394                              <1> 	;	   via 'ppoke'.
   395                              <1> 	;	4) If the dismountable file system's super block has been
   396                              <1> 	;	   modified, it is written out to the specified device
   397                              <1> 	;	   via 'ppoke'.
   398                              <1> 	;	5) A check is made if user's time quantum (uquant) ran out
   399                              <1> 	;	   during his execution. If so, 'tswap' is called to give
   400                              <1> 	;	   another user a chance to run.
   401                              <1> 	;	6) 'sysret' now goes into 'sysrele'.
   402                              <1> 	;	    (See 'sysrele' for conclusion.)

   690                              <1> sysexit: ; <terminate process>
   691                              <1> 	; 08/01/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
   692                              <1> 	; 22/08/2024
   693                              <1> 	; 20/08/2024
   694                              <1> 	; 18/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
   695                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022
   696                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
   697                              <1> 	; 14/11/2017
   698                              <1> 	; 27/05/2017
   699                              <1> 	; 10/04/2017
   700                              <1> 	; 26/02/2017 - 28/02/2017
   701                              <1> 	; 02/01/2017 - 23/01/2017
   702                              <1> 	; 06/06/2016 - 10/06/2016
   703                              <1> 	; 19/05/2016 - 23/05/2016
   704                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
   705                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 - 01/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
   706                              <1> 	; 19/04/2013 - 14/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
   707                              <1> 	;
   708                              <1> 	; 'sysexit' terminates a process. First each file that
   709                              <1> 	; the process has opened is closed by 'flose'. The process
   710                              <1> 	; status is then set to unused. The 'p.pid' table is then
   711                              <1> 	; searched to find children of the dying process. If any of
   712                              <1> 	; children are zombies (died by not waited for), they are
   713                              <1> 	; set free. The 'p.pid' table is then searched to find the
   714                              <1> 	; dying process's parent. When the parent is found, it is
   715                              <1> 	; checked to see if it is free or it is a zombie. If it is
   716                              <1> 	; one of these, the dying process just dies. If it is waiting
   717                              <1> 	; for a child process to die, it notified that it doesn't
   718                              <1> 	; have to wait anymore by setting it's status from 2 to 1
   719                              <1> 	; (waiting to active). It is awakened and put on runq by
   720                              <1> 	; 'putlu'. The dying process enters a zombie state in which
   721                              <1> 	; it will never be run again but stays around until a 'wait'
   722                              <1> 	; is completed by it's parent process. If the parent is not
   723                              <1> 	; found, process just dies. This means 'swap' is called with
   724                              <1> 	; 'u.uno=0'. What this does is the 'wswap' is not called
   725                              <1> 	; to write out the process and 'rswap' reads the new process
   726                              <1> 	; over the one that dies..i.e., the dying process is 
   727                              <1> 	; overwritten and destroyed.
   728                              <1>  	;
   729                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
   730                              <1> 	;	sysexit or conditional branch.
   731                              <1> 	; Arguments:
   732                              <1> 	;	-
   733                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
   734                              <1> 	;
   735                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
   736                              <1> 	;       System call number (=1) is in EAX register.
   737                              <1> 	;
   738                              <1> 	;       Other parameters are in EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP
   739                              <1> 	;       registers depending of function details.
   740                              <1> 	;
   741                              <1> 	; ('swap' procedure is mostly different than original UNIX v1.)
   742                              <1> 	;
   743                              <1> ; / terminate process
   744                              <1> 	; AX = 1
   745                              <1> 	;dec 	ax ; 0
   746                              <1> 	; 18/08/2024
   747 0000E275 48                  <1> 	dec	eax
   748 0000E276 66A3[42B00100]      <1> 	mov	[u.intr], ax ; 0
   749                              <1> 		; clr u.intr / clear interrupt control word
   750                              <1> 		; clr r1 / clear r1
   751                              <1> 	; 18/08/2024 - exit code (in EBX, BL)
   752 0000E27C 881D[76B00100]      <1> 	mov	[u.exit], bl

  1040                              <1> syswait: ; < wait for a processs to die >
  1041                              <1> 	; 20/08/2024
  1042                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022
  1043                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
  1044                              <1> 	; 17/09/2015
  1045                              <1> 	; 02/09/2015
  1046                              <1> 	; 01/09/2015
  1047                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  1048                              <1> 	; 24/05/2013 - 05/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  1049                              <1> 	;
  1050                              <1> 	; 'syswait' waits for a process die.
  1051                              <1> 	; It works in following way:
  1052                              <1> 	;    1) From the parent process number, the parent's
  1053                              <1> 	; 	process name is found. The p.ppid table of parent
  1054                              <1> 	;	names is then searched for this process name.
  1055                              <1> 	;	If a match occurs, r2 contains child's process
  1056                              <1> 	;	number. The child status is checked to see if it is
  1057                              <1> 	;	a zombie, i.e; dead but not waited for (p.stat=3)
  1058                              <1> 	;	If it is, the child process is freed and it's name
  1059                              <1> 	;	is put in (u.r0). A return is then made via 'sysret'.
  1060                              <1> 	;	If the child is not a zombie, nothing happens and
  1061                              <1> 	;	the search goes on through the p.ppid table until
  1062                              <1> 	;	all processes are checked or a zombie is found.
  1063                              <1> 	;    2) If no zombies are found, a check is made to see if
  1064                              <1> 	;	there are any children at all. If there are none,
  1065                              <1> 	;	an error return is made. If there are, the parent's
  1066                              <1> 	;	status is set to 2 (waiting for child to die),
  1067                              <1> 	;	the parent is swapped out, and a branch to 'syswait'
  1068                              <1> 	;	is made to wait on the next process.
  1069                              <1> 	;
  1070                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  1071                              <1> 	;	?
  1072                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  1073                              <1> 	;	-
  1074                              <1> 	; Inputs: -
  1075                              <1> 	; Outputs: if zombie found, it's name put in u.r0.
  1076                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  1077                              <1> 	;
  1078                              <1> 
  1079                              <1> ; / wait for a process to die
  1080                              <1> 
  1081                              <1> syswait_0:
  1082 0000E401 0FB61D[47B00100]    <1> 	movzx	ebx, byte [u.uno] ; 01/09/2015
  1083                              <1> 		; movb u.uno,r1 / put parents process number in r1
  1084 0000E408 D0E3                <1> 	shl	bl, 1
  1085                              <1> 	;shl	bx, 1
  1086                              <1> 		; asl r1 / x2 to get index into p.pid table
  1087 0000E40A 668B83[F0AE0100]    <1> 	mov	ax, [ebx+p.pid-2]
  1088                              <1> 		; mov p.pid-2(r1),r1 / get the name of this process
  1089 0000E411 31F6                <1> 	xor	esi, esi
  1090                              <1> 		; clr r2
  1091 0000E413 31C9                <1> 	xor	ecx, ecx ; 30/10/2013
  1092                              <1> 	;xor	cl, cl
  1093                              <1> 		; clr r3 / initialize reg 3
  1094                              <1> syswait_1: ; 1:
  1095                              <1> 	;add	si, 2
  1096                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022
  1097 0000E415 46                  <1> 	inc	esi
  1098 0000E416 46                  <1> 	inc	esi
  1099                              <1> 		; add $2,r2 / use r2 for index into p.ppid table
  1100                              <1> 			  ; / search table of parent processes
  1101                              <1> 			  ; / for this process name
  1102 0000E417 663B86[10AF0100]    <1> 	cmp	ax, [esi+p.ppid-2]
  1103                              <1> 		; cmp p.ppid-2(r2),r1 / r2 will contain the childs
  1104                              <1> 			            ; / process number
  1105 0000E41E 7542                <1> 	jne	short syswait_3
  1106                              <1> 		;bne 3f / branch if no match of parent process name

  1210                              <1> sysfork: ; < create a new process >
  1211                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.1.0 
  1212                              <1> 	; 12/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.11 (u.cdrv, u.cdir)
  1213                              <1> 	; 19/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9 (STDIN/STDOUT)
  1214                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
  1215                              <1> 	; 02/01/2017 (TRDOS 386 modification)
  1216                              <1> 	; 04/09/2015 - 18/05/2015
  1217                              <1> 	; 28/08/2015 - 01/09/2015 - 02/09/2015
  1218                              <1> 	; 09/05/2015 - 10/05/2015 - 14/05/2015
  1219                              <1> 	; 06/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  1220                              <1> 	; 24/05/2013 - 14/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  1221                              <1> 	;
  1222                              <1> 	; 'sysfork' creates a new process. This process is referred
  1223                              <1> 	; to as the child process. This new process core image is
  1224                              <1> 	; a copy of that of the caller of 'sysfork'. The only
  1225                              <1> 	; distinction is the return location and the fact that (u.r0)
  1226                              <1> 	; in the old process (parent) contains the process id (p.pid)
  1227                              <1> 	; of the new process (child). This id is used by 'syswait'.
  1228                              <1> 	; 'sysfork' works in the following manner:
  1229                              <1> 	;    1) The process status table (p.stat) is searched to find
  1230                              <1> 	;	a process number that is unused. If none are found
  1231                              <1> 	;	an error occurs.
  1232                              <1> 	;    2) when one is found, it becomes the child process number
  1233                              <1> 	;	and it's status (p.stat) is set to active.
  1234                              <1> 	;    3) If the parent had a control tty, the interrupt
  1235                              <1> 	;	character in that tty buffer is cleared.
  1236                              <1> 	;    4) The child process is put on the lowest priority run
  1237                              <1> 	;	queue via 'putlu'.
  1238                              <1> 	;    5) A new process name is gotten from 'mpid' (actually
  1239                              <1> 	;	it is a unique number) and is put in the child's unique
  1240                              <1> 	;	identifier; process id (p.pid).
  1241                              <1> 	;    6) The process name of the parent is then obtained and
  1242                              <1> 	;	placed in the unique identifier of the parent process
  1243                              <1> 	;	name is then put in 'u.r0'.
  1244                              <1> 	;    7) The child process is then written out on disk by
  1245                              <1> 	;	'wswap',i.e., the parent process is copied onto disk
  1246                              <1> 	;	and the child is born. (The child process is written
  1247                              <1> 	;	out on disk/drum with 'u.uno' being the child process
  1248                              <1> 	;	number.)
  1249                              <1> 	;    8) The parent process number is then restored to 'u.uno'.
  1250                              <1> 	;    9) The child process name is put in 'u.r0'.
  1251                              <1> 	;   10) The pc on the stack sp + 18 is incremented by 2 to
  1252                              <1> 	;	create the return address for the parent process.
  1253                              <1> 	;   11) The 'u.fp' list as then searched to see what files
  1254                              <1> 	;	the parent has opened. For each file the parent has
  1255                              <1> 	;	opened, the corresponding 'fsp' entry must be updated
  1256                              <1> 	;	to indicate that the child process also has opened
  1257                              <1> 	;	the file. A branch to 'sysret' is then made.
  1258                              <1> 	;
  1259                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  1260                              <1> 	;	from shell ?
  1261                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  1262                              <1> 	;	-
  1263                              <1> 	; Inputs: -
  1264                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - child process name
  1265                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  1266                              <1> 	;	
  1267                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
  1268                              <1> 	;	AX = r0 = PID (>0) (at the return of 'sysfork')
  1269                              <1> 	;	= process id of child a parent process returns
  1270                              <1> 	;	= process id of parent when a child process returns
  1271                              <1> 	;
  1272                              <1> 	;       In original UNIX v1, sysfork is called and returns as
  1273                              <1> 	;	in following manner: (with an example: c library, fork)
  1274                              <1> 	;
  1275                              <1> 	;	1:
  1276                              <1> 	;		sys	fork
  1277                              <1> 	;			br 1f  / child process returns here
  1278                              <1> 	;		bes	2f     / parent process returns here
  1279                              <1> 	;		/ pid of new process in r0
  1280                              <1> 	;		rts	pc
  1281                              <1> 	;	2: / parent process condionally branches here
  1282                              <1> 	;		mov	$-1,r0 / pid = -1 means error return
  1283                              <1> 	;		rts	pc
  1284                              <1> 	;
  1285                              <1> 	;	1: / child process brances here
  1286                              <1> 	;		clr	r0   / pid = 0 in child process
  1287                              <1> 	;		rts	pc
  1288                              <1> 	;
  1289                              <1> 	;	In UNIX v7x86 (386) by Robert Nordier (1999)
  1290                              <1> 	;		// pid = fork();
  1291                              <1> 	;		//
  1292                              <1> 	;		// pid == 0 in child process;
  1293                              <1> 	;		// pid == -1 means error return
  1294                              <1> 	;		// in child,
  1295                              <1> 	;		//	parents id is in par_uid if needed
  1296                              <1> 	;
  1297                              <1> 	;		_fork:
  1298                              <1> 	;			mov	$.fork,eax
  1299                              <1> 	;			int	$0x30
  1300                              <1> 	;			jmp	1f
  1301                              <1> 	;			jnc	2f
  1302                              <1> 	;			jmp	cerror
  1303                              <1> 	;		1:
  1304                              <1> 	;			mov	eax,_par_uid
  1305                              <1> 	;			xor	eax,eax
  1306                              <1> 	;		2:
  1307                              <1> 	;			ret
  1308                              <1> 	;
  1309                              <1> 	;	In Retro UNIX 8086 v1,
  1310                              <1> 	;	'sysfork' returns in following manner:
  1311                              <1> 	;
  1312                              <1> 	;		mov	ax, sys_fork
  1313                              <1> 	;		mov	bx, offset @f ; routine for child
  1314                              <1> 	;		int	20h

  1319                              <1> 	;		jmp	next_routine_for_parent
  1320                              <1> 	;
  1321                              <1> 	;	@@: ; routine for child process here
  1322                              <1> 	;		....
  1323                              <1> 	;	NOTE: 'sysfork' returns to specified offset
  1324                              <1> 	;	       for child process by using BX input.
  1325                              <1> 	;	      (at first, parent process will return then
  1326                              <1> 	;	      child process will return -after swapped in-
  1327                              <1> 	;	      'syswait' is needed in parent process
  1328                              <1> 	;	      if return from child process will be waited for.)
  1329                              <1> 	;
  1330                              <1> 
  1331                              <1> ; / create a new process
  1332                              <1> 	; EBX = return address for child process
  1333                              <1> 	     ; (Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification !)

  1550                              <1> syscreat: ; < create file >
  1551                              <1> 	; 05/09/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0
  1552                              <1> 	; 15/01/2026
  1553                              <1> 	; 13/01/2026

  1555                              <1> 	; 06/08/2025
  1556                              <1> 	; 05/08/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  1557                              <1> 	;	(Major Modification)
  1558                              <1> 	; 29/08/2024
  1559                              <1> 	; 25/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
  1560                              <1> 	; 08/08/2022
  1561                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
  1562                              <1> 	; 13/11/2017
  1563                              <1> 	; 27/10/2016
  1564                              <1> 	; 25/10/2016 - 26/10/2016
  1565                              <1> 	; 15/10/2016 - 16/10/2016 - 17/10/2016
  1566                              <1> 	; 10/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  1567                              <1> 	;	     -derived from INT_21H.ASM-
  1568                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_create_file")
  1569                              <1>         ; 	10/07/2011 (12/03/2011)
  1570                              <1>         ;	INT 21h Function AH = 3Ch
  1571                              <1>         ;	Create File
  1572                              <1>         ;	INPUT
  1573                              <1>         ;	   CX = Attributes
  1574                              <1>         ;          DS:DX= Address of zero terminaned path name
  1575                              <1>         ;
  1576                              <1> 	; 27/12/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1.1)
  1577                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  1578                              <1> 	; 27/05/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  1579                              <1> 	;
  1580                              <1> 	; 'syscreat' called with two arguments; name and mode.
  1581                              <1> 	; u.namep points to name of the file and mode is put
  1582                              <1> 	; on the stack. 'namei' is called to get i-number of the file.
  1583                              <1> 	; If the file aready exists, it's mode and owner remain 
  1584                              <1> 	; unchanged, but it is truncated to zero length. If the file
  1585                              <1> 	; did not exist, an i-node is created with the new mode via
  1586                              <1> 	; 'maknod' whether or not the file already existed, it is
  1587                              <1> 	; open for writing. The fsp table is then searched for a free
  1588                              <1> 	; entry. When a free entry is found, proper data is placed
  1589                              <1> 	; in it and the number of this entry is put in the u.fp list.
  1590                              <1> 	; The index to the u.fp (also know as the file descriptor)
  1591                              <1> 	; is put in the user's r0.
  1592                              <1> 	;
  1593                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  1594                              <1> 	;	syscreate; name; mode
  1595                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  1596                              <1> 	;	name - name of the file to be created
  1597                              <1> 	;	mode - mode of the file to be created
  1598                              <1> 	; Inputs: (arguments)
  1599                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - index to u.fp list 
  1600                              <1> 	;		   (the file descriptor of new file)
  1601                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  1602                              <1> 	;
  1603                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  1604                              <1> 	;       'syscreate' system call has two arguments; so,
  1605                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, name is pointed to by BX register
  1606                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, mode is in CX register
  1607                              <1> 	;
  1608                              <1> 	;	AX register (will be restored via 'u.r0') will return
  1609                              <1> 	;	to the user with the file descriptor/number
  1610                              <1> 	;	(index to u.fp list).
  1611                              <1> 	;
  1612                              <1> 	;call	arg2
  1613                              <1> 	; * name - 'u.namep' points to address of file/path name
  1614                              <1> 	;          in the user's program segment ('u.segmnt')
  1615                              <1> 	;          with offset in BX register (as sysopen argument 1).
  1616                              <1> 	; * mode - sysopen argument 2 is in CX register 
  1617                              <1> 	;          which is on top of stack.
  1618                              <1> 	;
  1619                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (10/10/2016)
  1620                              <1> 	;
  1621                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  1622                              <1>         ;	   CL = File Attributes
  1623                              <1> 	;     	      bit 0 (1) - Read only file (R)
  1624                              <1> 	;             bit 1 (1) - Hidden file (H)
  1625                              <1>         ;             bit 2 (1) - System file (R)
  1626                              <1> 	;             bit 3 (1) - Volume label/name (V)
  1627                              <1>         ;             bit 4 (1) - Subdirectory (D)
  1628                              <1> 	;	      bit 5 (1) - File has been archived (A)
  1629                              <1>         ;          EBX = Pointer to filename (ASCIIZ) -path-
  1630                              <1> 	;
  1631                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  1632                              <1> 	;          eax = File/Device Handle/Number (index) (AL)
  1633                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
  1634                              <1> 	;
  1635                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
  1636                              <1> 	;
  1637                              <1> 	; Note: If the file is existing and it has not any one
  1638                              <1> 	;	of S,H,R,V,D attributes, it will be truncated
  1639                              <1> 	;	to zero length; otherwise, access error will be
  1640                              <1> 	;	returned.

  2034                              <1> 	; 06/10/2016, 07/10/2016, 08/10/2016
  2035                              <1> 	; 05/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  2036                              <1> 	;	     -derived from INT_21H.ASM-
  2037                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_open_file")
  2038                              <1>         ; 	26/02/2011 
  2039                              <1>         ;	INT 21h Function AH = 3Dh
  2040                              <1>         ;	Open File
  2041                              <1>         ;	INPUT
  2042                              <1>         ;	   AL= File Access Value
  2043                              <1> 	;     	     0- Open for reading
  2044                              <1> 	;            1- Open for writing
  2045                              <1>         ;            2- Open for reading and writing
  2046                              <1>         ;          DS:DX= Pointer to filename (ASCIIZ)
  2047                              <1>         ;
  2048                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  2049                              <1> 	; 22/05/2013 - 27/05/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  2050                              <1> 	;
  2051                              <1> 	; 'sysopen' opens a file in following manner:
  2052                              <1> 	;    1) The second argument in a sysopen says whether to
  2053                              <1> 	;	open the file ro read (0) or write (>0).
  2054                              <1> 	;    2) I-node of the particular file is obtained via 'namei'.
  2055                              <1> 	;    3) The file is opened by 'iopen'.
  2056                              <1> 	;    4) Next housekeeping is performed on the fsp table
  2057                              <1> 	;	and the user's open file list - u.fp.
  2058                              <1> 	;	a) u.fp and fsp are scanned for the next available slot.
  2059                              <1> 	;	b) An entry for the file is created in the fsp table.
  2060                              <1> 	;	c) The number of this entry is put on u.fp list.
  2061                              <1> 	;	d) The file descriptor index to u.fp list is pointed
  2062                              <1> 	;	   to by u.r0.
  2063                              <1> 	;
  2064                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  2065                              <1> 	;	sysopen; name; mode
  2066                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  2067                              <1> 	;	name - file name or path name
  2068                              <1> 	;	mode - 0 to open for reading
  2069                              <1> 	;	       1 to open for writing
  2070                              <1> 	; Inputs: (arguments)
  2071                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - index to u.fp list (the file descriptor)
  2072                              <1> 	;		  is put into r0's location on the stack.
  2073                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  2074                              <1> 	;
  2075                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  2076                              <1> 	;       'sysopen' system call has two arguments; so,
  2077                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, name is pointed to by BX register
  2078                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, mode is in CX register
  2079                              <1> 	;
  2080                              <1> 	;	AX register (will be restored via 'u.r0') will return
  2081                              <1> 	;	to the user with the file descriptor/number
  2082                              <1> 	;	(index to u.fp list).
  2083                              <1> 	;
  2084                              <1> 	;call	arg2
  2085                              <1> 	; * name - 'u.namep' points to address of file/path name
  2086                              <1> 	;          in the user's program segment ('u.segmnt')
  2087                              <1> 	;          with offset in BX register (as sysopen argument 1).
  2088                              <1> 	; * mode - sysopen argument 2 is in CX register
  2089                              <1> 	;          which is on top of stack.
  2090                              <1> 	;
  2091                              <1> 	; jsr r0,arg2 / get sys args into u.namep and on stack
  2092                              <1> 	;
  2093                              <1>        	; system call registers: ebx, ecx (through 'sysenter')
  2094                              <1> 	;
  2095                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (05/10/2016)
  2096                              <1> 	;
  2097                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  2098                              <1>         ;	   CL = File Access Value (Open Mode)
  2099                              <1> 	;     	      0 - Open file for reading
  2100                              <1> 	;             1 - Open file for writing
  2101                              <1>         ;             2 - Open device for reading
  2102                              <1> 	;	      3 - Open device for writing
  2103                              <1>         ;          EBX = Pointer to filename/devicename (ASCIIZ)
  2104                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  2105                              <1> 	;          eax = File/Device Handle/Number (index) (AL)
  2106                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
  2107                              <1> 	;
  2108                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
  2109                              <1> 	;
  2110                              <1> 
  2111 0000E6DF 80F901              <1> 	cmp	cl, 1 ; read file (0), write file (1)
  2112 0000E6E2 7614                <1> 	jna	short sysopen_0

  2753                              <1>         ;          DS:DX= Buffer address
  2754                              <1>         ;
  2755                              <1> 	; Note: TRDOS 386 'sysread' has been derived from
  2756                              <1> 	;	Retro UNIX 386 v1 'sysread', except a few
  2757                              <1> 	;	code modifications.

  2760                              <1> 	; 11/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  2761                              <1> 	; 23/05/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  2762                              <1> 	;
  2763                              <1> 	; 'sysread' is given a buffer to read into and the number of
  2764                              <1> 	; characters to be read. If finds the file from the file
  2765                              <1> 	; descriptor located in *u.r0 (r0). This file descriptor
  2766                              <1> 	; is returned from a successful open call (sysopen).
  2767                              <1> 	; The i-number of file is obtained via 'rw1' and the data
  2768                              <1> 	; is read into core via 'readi'.
  2769                              <1> 	;
  2770                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  2771                              <1> 	;	sysread; buffer; nchars
  2772                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  2773                              <1> 	;	buffer - location of contiguous bytes where
  2774                              <1> 	;		 input will be placed.
  2775                              <1> 	;	nchars - number of bytes or characters to be read.
  2776                              <1> 	; Inputs: *u.r0 - file descriptor (& arguments)
  2777                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - number of bytes read.
  2778                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  2779                              <1> 	;
  2780                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  2781                              <1> 	;       'sysread' system call has three arguments; so,
  2782                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, file descriptor is in BX register
  2783                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, buffer address/offset in CX register
  2784                              <1> 	;	* 3rd argument, number of bytes is in DX register
  2785                              <1> 	;

  2787                              <1> 	;	to the user with number of bytes read.
  2788                              <1> 	;
  2789                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (05/10/2016)
  2790                              <1> 	;
  2791                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  2792                              <1>         ;	   EBX = File handle (descriptor/index)
  2793                              <1> 	;	   ECX = Buffer address
  2794                              <1>         ;          EDX = Number of bytes
  2795                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  2796                              <1> 	;          EAX = Number of bytes have been read
  2797                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
  2798                              <1> 	;
  2799                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)

  2870                              <1> 	;

  2872                              <1> 	; and the number of characters to write. If finds the file

  2877                              <1> 	;
  2878                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  2879                              <1> 	;	syswrite; buffer; nchars
  2880                              <1> 	; Arguments:

  2882                              <1> 	;	nchars - number of characters to be written.

  2885                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  2886                              <1> 	;
  2887                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  2888                              <1> 	;       'syswrite' system call has three arguments; so,
  2889                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, file descriptor is in BX register
  2890                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, buffer address/offset in CX register
  2891                              <1> 	;	* 3rd argument, number of bytes is in DX register
  2892                              <1> 	;

  2894                              <1> 	;	to the user with number of bytes written.

  2896                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  2897                              <1>         ;	   EBX = File handle (descriptor/index)

  3126                              <1> systimer:
  3127                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
  3128                              <1> 	; 02/01/2017
  3129                              <1> 	; 21/12/2016
  3130                              <1> 	; 19/12/2016
  3131                              <1> 	; 10/12/2016 (callback)
  3132                              <1> 	; 10/06/2016
  3133                              <1> 	; 07/06/2016
  3134                              <1> 	; 06/06/2016
  3135                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016
  3136                              <1> 	; 19/05/2016
  3137                              <1> 	; 18/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
  3138                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
  3139                              <1> 	;
  3140                              <1> 	; (start or stop timer event(s))
  3141                              <1> 	;
  3142                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  3143                              <1> 	;	BL = Signal return byte (response byte)
  3144                              <1> 	;	     (Any requested value between 0 and 255)
  3145                              <1> 	;	     (Kernel will put it at the requested address)
  3146                              <1> 	;	BH = Time count unit
  3147                              <1> 	;	     0 = Stop timer event
  3148                              <1> 	;	     1 = 18.2 ticks per second
  3149                              <1> 	;	     2 = 10 milliseconds
  3150                              <1> 	;	     3 = 1 second (for real time clock interrupt)
  3151                              <1> 	;	     4 = time/tick count in current time count unit
  3152                              <1> 	;	    // 10/12/2016
  3153                              <1> 	;	    80h = Stop timer event (callback method)
  3154                              <1> 	;	    81h = 18.2 ticks per second, callback method
  3155                              <1> 	;	    82h = 10 milliseconds, callback method
  3156                              <1> 	;	    83h = 1 second (for RTC int), callback method
  3157                              <1> 	;	    84h = current time count unit, callback method
  3158                              <1> 	;
  3159                              <1> 	;	    Note: Only 03h or 83h will set real time clock
  3160                              <1> 	;		  (RTC) events (Others are for PIT events)!
  3161                              <1> 	;
  3162                              <1> 	;	NOTE: If callback (user service) method is used,
  3163                              <1> 	;	    EDX will point to the return address (of service
  3164                              <1> 	;	    procedure) in user's space instead of signal
  3165                              <1> 	;	    response byte address. (TRDOS 386 kernel will
  3166                              <1> 	;	    direct the cpu to that address -in user's space-
  3167                              <1> 	;	    at the return of system call or interrupt 
  3168                              <1> 	;	    just after the adjusted count/time is elapsed.)
  3169                              <1> 	;	    User's sevice routine must be ended with a
  3170                              <1> 	;	    'iret'. Normal return addresses from system
  3171                              <1> 	;	    calls or and interrupts will be kept same except
  3172                              <1> 	;	    the timer returns.
  3173                              <1>      	;
  3174                              <1> 	;	BH = 0 -> Stop timer event
  3175                              <1> 	;	BL = Timer event number (1 to 255) if BH = 0
  3176                              <1> 	;	     If BL = 0, all timer events (which are belongs
  3177                              <1> 	;	      to running process) will be stopped
  3178                              <1> 	;	ECX = Time/Tick count (depending on time count unit)
  3179                              <1> 	;	EDX = Signal return (Response) byte address
  3180                              <1> 	;	      (virtual address in user's memory space)
  3181                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  3182                              <1> 	;	AL = Timer event number	(1 to 255) (max. value = 16)
  3183                              <1> 	;	IF BH Input = 0 & CF = 0 & AL = 0 ->
  3184                              <1> 	;	     timer event(s) has/have been stopped/finished
  3185                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 & AL = 0 -> no timer setting space to set
  3186                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 & AL > 0 -> timer count unit is not usable
  3187                              <1> 	;
  3188                              <1> 	;	NOTE: To modify a time count for a user function,
  3189                              <1> 	;	      at first, current timer event must be stopped
  3190                              <1> 	;	      then a new timer event (which is related with
  3191                              <1> 	;	      same user function) must be started.
  3192                              <1> 	;
  3193                              <1> 	;	      Signal return (response) byte may be used for
  3194                              <1> 	;	      several purposes. Kernel will put this value
  3195                              <1> 	;	      to requested address during timer interrupt,
  3196                              <1> 	;	      program/user can check this value to understand
  3197                              <1> 	;	      which event has been occurred and what is changed.
  3198                              <1> 	;	      (Multi timer events can share same signal address)
  3199                              <1> 	;
  3200                              <1> 	;	NOTE: If the process is running while the time count
  3201                              <1> 	;	      is reached, kernel will put signal return (response)
  3202                              <1> 	;	      byte value at requested address during timer
  3203                              <1> 	;	      interrupt and the process will continue to run.
  3204                              <1> 	;	      Program/process must call (jump to) it's timer event
  3205                              <1> 	;	      function as required, for checking the timer event
  3206                              <1> 	;	      status via signal return (response) byte address.
  3207                              <1> 	;
  3208                              <1> 	;	      If the process is not running (waiting or sleeping
  3209                              <1> 	;	      or released) while the time count is reached,
  3210                              <1> 	;	      it is restarted from where it left, to ensure
  3211                              <1> 	;	      proper multi media (video, audio, clock, timer)
  3212                              <1> 	;	      functionality.
  3213                              <1> 	;
  3214                              <1> 	;	      (It is better to use 'syswait' or 'syssleep',
  3215                              <1> 	;	      or 'sysrele' system call just after the timer
  3216                              <1> 	;	      function. Otherwise, timer events may block other
  3217                              <1> 	;	      processes which are not using timer events.)
  3218                              <1> 	;
  3219                              <1> 	; Timer Event Structure: (max. 16 timer events, 16*16 bytes)
  3220                              <1> 	;       Owner:	        resb 1 ; 0 = free
  3221                              <1> 	;		  	       ;>0 = process number (u.uno)
  3222                              <1> 	;	Calback:	resb 1 ; 1 = callback, 0 = response byte
  3223                              <1> 	;	Interrupt:      resb 1 ; 0 = Timer interrupt (or none)
  3224                              <1> 	;		   	       ; 1 = Real Time Clock interrupt
  3225                              <1> 	;	Response:       resb 1 ; 0 to 255, signal return value
  3226                              <1> 	;	Count Limit:	resd 1 ; count of ticks (total/set)
  3227                              <1> 	;	Current Count: 	resd 1 ; count of ticks (current)
  3228                              <1> 	;	Response Addr:  resd 1 ; response byte (pointer) address
  3229                              <1> 	;
  3230                              <1> 
  3231                              <1> 	; 19/12/2016 (timer callback)
  3232 0000E9CD C605[A0A80100]00    <1> 	mov	byte [tcallback], 0
  3233 0000E9D4 C605[A1A80100]00    <1> 	mov	byte [trtc], 0
  3234 0000E9DB C705[6CB00100]0000- <1> 	mov	dword [u.tcb], 0 ; this is not necessary...
  3234 0000E9E3 0000                <1>
  3235                              <1> 
  3236 0000E9E5 80FF80              <1> 	cmp	bh, 80h
  3237 0000E9E8 7224                <1> 	jb	short systimer_cb2
