  3507                              <1> 	; 16/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
  3508                              <1> 	;
  3509                              <1> 	; VIDEO DATA TRANSFER FUNCTIONS:
  3510                              <1> 	;
  3511                              <1> 	; Inputs:
  3512                              <1> 	;		; 07/02/2021
  3513                              <1> 	;	BH = 0 = VIDEO BIOS Mode 3, tty/text mode data transfers
  3514                              <1> 	;	     BL =
  3515                              <1> 	;		Bits 0&1, Transfer direction
  3516                              <1> 	;	     	 	0 - System to system
  3517                              <1> 	;			1 - User to system
  3518                              <1> 	;			2 - System to user
  3519                              <1> 	;			3 - Exhange (Swap) - 28/01/2021
  3520                              <1> 	;		Bits 2, Transfer Type
  3521                              <1> 	;			0 - Display page (complete) transfer
  3522                              <1> 	;	     		1 - Display page window (col,row) transfer
  3523                              <1> 	;		; 28/01/2021
  3524                              <1> 	;		Bits 3..7 - Reserved, undefined (must be 0)
  3525                              <1> 	;	        ; 28/01/2021
  3526                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 0 -> System to system (display page) transfer
  3527                              <1> 	;		 CL = Source page (0FFh = current video page)
  3528                              <1> 	;		 DL = Destination page (0FFh = current video page)
  3529                              <1> 	;		 (Note: Nothing to do if src & dest are same page)
  3530                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 1&2 -> user to system & system to user transfer
  3531                              <1> 	;		 ECX = User's buffer address
  3532                              <1> 	;		 DL = Video page (0FFh = current video page)
  3533                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 3 -> exchange (swap) display page ; 28/01/2021
  3534                              <1> 	;		 ECX = User's buffer address
  3535                              <1> 	;		 DL = Video page (0FFh = current video page)
  3536                              <1> 	;		 EDI = Swap address in user's memory (must be > 0)
  3537                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 5&6&7 -> user to system, system to user transfer
  3538                              <1> 	;		(system window is in current/active display page)
  3539                              <1> 	;		 ESI = User's buffer address
  3540                              <1> 	;		 ECX Low 16 bits = Top left column (X1 position)
  3541                              <1> 	;		 ECX High 16 bits = Top row (Y1 position)
  3542                              <1> 	;		 EDX Low 16 bits = Bottom right column (X2 position)
  3543                              <1> 	;		 EDX High 16 bits = Bottom row (Y2 position)
  3544                              <1>         ;                If BL = 5 or BL bit 0 & bit 1 are 1 ; 28/01/2021
  3545                              <1> 	;		 EDI = Swap address (in user's memory space)
  3546                              <1> 	;		 (If swap address > 0, previous content of the window
  3547                              <1> 	;		 will be saved into swap area in user's memory space)
  3548                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 4 -> system to system transfer
  3549                              <1> 	;		 ESI = System's source buffer (video page) address
  3550                              <1> 	;		 ECX Low 16 bits = Top left column (X1 position)
  3551                              <1> 	;		 ECX High 16 bits = Top row (Y1 position)
  3552                              <1> 	;		 EDX Low 16 bits = Bottom right column (X2 position)
  3553                              <1> 	;		 EDX High 16 bits = Bottom row (Y2 position)
  3554                              <1> 	;		 EDI = System's destination buffer (video page) addr
  3555                              <1> 	;
  3556                              <1> 	;		; 06/02/2021
  3557                              <1> 	;		; 05/02/2021
  3558                              <1> 	;		; 01/02/2021, 02/02/2021
  3559                              <1> 	;		; 30/01/2021, 31/02/2021
  3560                              <1> 	;		; 29/01/2021 (major modification)
  3561                              <1> 	;		; 23/11/2020 (major modification)
  3562                              <1> 	;		; 22/11/2020 (bugfixes and extensions)
  3563                              <1> 	;	BH = 1 = VGA Graphics (0A0000h) data transfers
  3564                              <1> 	;		BL bit 7
  3565                              <1> 	;		   resolution (screen width) option
  3566                              <1> 	;		   0 = 320 pixels
  3567                              <1> 	;		   1 = 640 pixels
  3568                              <1> 	;		.. followings are same with SVGA transfer function
  3569                              <1> 	;		BL bit 6
  3570                              <1> 	;		   direction option
  3571                              <1> 	;		   0 = user to system (video memory)
  3572                              <1> 	;		   1 = system to user
  3573                              <1> 	;		BL bit 5
  3574                              <1> 	;		   masked/direct (non-masked) operations
  3575                              <1> 	;		   1 = masked, 0 = non-masked (direct)
  3576                              <1> 	;		BL bit 4
  3577                              <1> 	;		   page/window option
  3578                              <1> 	;		   1 = window, 0 = display page (screen)
  3579                              <1> 	;		BL bit 0 to 3 (pixel operation types)
  3580                              <1> 	;		   0 = Copy pixels (colors) ((mask color))
  3581                              <1> 	;		   1 = Change (New, Fill) color
  3582                              <1> 	;		   2 = Add color
  3583                              <1> 	;		   3 = Sub color
  3584                              <1> 	;		   4 = OR color
  3585                              <1> 	;		   5 = AND color
  3586                              <1> 	;		   6 = XOR color
  3587                              <1> 	;		   7 = NOT color
  3588                              <1> 	;		   8 = NEG color
  3589                              <1> 	;		   9 = INC color
  3590                              <1> 	;		  10 = DEC color
  3591                              <1> 	;		  11 = Mix (Average) colors
  3592                              <1> 	;		  12 = Replace pixel colors
  3593                              <1> 	;		  13 = Copy pixel block(s)
  3594                              <1> 	;		  14 = Write line(s)
  3595                              <1> 	;		  15 = Write character (font)
  3596                              <1> 	;
  3597                              <1> 	;	   Input Registers for pixel operations:
  3598                              <1> 	;		 Same with LFB data transfer function below
  3599                              <1> 	;
  3600                              <1> 	;		; 25/02/2021
  3601                              <1> 	;		; 05/02/2021, 06/02/2021
  3602                              <1> 	;		; 01/02/2021, 02/02/2021
  3603                              <1> 	;		; 30/01/2021, 31/02/2021
  3604                              <1> 	; 		; 29/01/2021 (major modification)
  3605                              <1> 	;		; 23/11/2020 (major modification)
  3606                              <1> 	;		; 22/11/2020 (bugfixes and extensions)
  3607                              <1> 	;	BH = 2 = Super VGA, LINEAR FRAME BUFFER data transfers
  3608                              <1> 	;		BL bit 7
  3609                              <1> 	;		   unused (invalid), must be 0
  3610                              <1> 	;		BL bit 6
  3611                              <1> 	;		   direction option
  3612                              <1> 	;		   0 = user to system (video memory)
  3613                              <1> 	;		   1 = system to user
  3614                              <1> 	;		BL bit 5
  3615                              <1> 	;		   masked/direct (non-masked) operations
  3616                              <1> 	;		   1 = masked, 0 = non-masked (direct)
  3617                              <1> 	;		BL bit 4
  3618                              <1> 	;		   page/window option
  3619                              <1> 	;		   1 = window, 0 = display page (screen)
  3620                              <1> 	;		BL bit 0 to 3 (pixel operation types)
  3621                              <1> 	;		   0 = Copy pixels (colors) ((mask color))

  3971                              <1> 	;	     * RGB (TRUE) colors to 256 colors conversion:
  3972                              <1>         ;             TRUE Colors -> 8,8,8 (R,G,B; byte 0 is R)
  3973                              <1> 	;	      256 colors -> 2,2,2,2 (R,G,B,L; bit 0&1 is R)
  3974                              <1> 	; 		  bit 6&7 -> luminosity base level (0,1,2,3)
  3975                              <1> 	;		  bit 4&5 -> blue level (0,1,2,3)
  3976                              <1> 	;		  bit 2%3 -> green level (0,1,2,3)
  3977                              <1> 	;		  bit 0&1 -> red level (0,1,2,3)
  3978                              <1> 	;	      Example: total red level : luminosity + red level
  3979                              <1> 	;	      Luminosity base level: 0 -> 16
  3980                              <1> 	;		 		     1 -> 32
  3981                              <1> 	;				     2 -> 64
  3982                              <1> 	;				     3 -> 128
  3983                              <1> 	;	      Color level:
  3984                              <1> 	;				    0 -> 0
  3985                              <1> 	;				    1 -> luminosity level
  3986                              <1> 	;				    2 -> luminosity level + 64
  3987                              <1> 	;				    3 -> 255
  3988                              <1> 	;	     Luminosity base level = min (R,G,B)
  3989                              <1> 	;			if it is <16, it will be set to 16
  3990                              <1> 	;	     Color levels: Color values are fixed to (nearest)
  3991                              <1> 	;		   one of all possible set level (step) values
  3992                              <1> 	;		   (according to luminosity base level); then
  3993                              <1> 	;		   color levels are set to R-L, G-L, B-L.
  3994                              <1> 	;	 For example: If luminosity base level is 32
  3995                              <1> 	;		  all possible set values are 0, 32, 96, 255.
  3996                              <1> 	;
  3997                              <1> 	;	    * RGB (TRUE) colors to 16 colors conversion:
  3998                              <1> 	;	    16 colors: R,B,G,L bits (4 bits)
  3999                              <1> 	;	    	   If any one of R,G,B >= 128 L = 1
  4000                              <1>  	;		   If max. value of (R,G,B) >= 32, it is 1
  4001                              <1> 	;		      else all color bits (R&G&B&L) are 0
  4002                              <1> 	;		   If the second value >= max. value / 2
  4003                              <1> 	;		      it is 1
  4004                              <1> 	;		   If the third value >= max. value / 2
  4005                              <1> 	;		      it is 1
  4006                              <1> 	;	    Example: R = 132, G = 64, B = 78
  4007                              <1> 	;		     L = 1, R = 1
  4008                              <1> 	;		     G < 66 --> G = 0
  4009                              <1> 	;		     B >= 66 --> B = 1

  4022                              <1> 	;			CX & EDX will not be used

  4026                              <1> 	;	    Above 11Fh, from 140h to 1FEh, it will be accepted
  4027                              <1> 	;	    as Bochs/Plex86 emulator video mode and it will be
  4028                              <1> 	;	    used only if [vbe3] = 2 and detected

  4091                              <1> 	; VIDEO MEMORY MAPPING:
  4092                              <1> 	;	BH = 10 = Map video memory to user's buffer
  4093                              <1> 	;
  4094                              <1> 	;	   BL = 0 : CGA memory (0B8000h) map (32K)
  4095                              <1> 	;	   BL = 1 : VGA memory (0A0000h) map (64K)

  4097                              <1> 	;

  4099                              <1> 	;	EDX = Buffer size in bytes (if BL = 2)

  4103                              <1> 	;	EBX = mapped (actual) size of video memory (bytes)
  4104                              <1> 	;	ECX = virtual start address of user's video buffer
  4105                              <1> 	;	EDX is same with EDX input
  4106                              <1> 	;
  4107                              <1> 	;	(Note: Memory page boundaries will be applied

  4116                              <1> 	; SET/READ COLOR PALETTE (set/read DAC color registers)
  4117                              <1> 	;	((256 colors (8bpp) VGA/CGA video hardware feature))
  4118                              <1> 	;
  4119                              <1> 	;	BH = 11 = Set/Read DAC color registers
  4120                              <1> 	;
  4121                              <1> 	;	   (BL<4 Original method for std VGA video hardware)
  4122                              <1> 	;	   BL = 0 : Read all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4123                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit colors, in RGB order)
  4124                              <1> 	;	   BL = 1 : Set all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4125                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit colors, in RGB order)
  4126                              <1> 	;	   BL = 2 : Read single DAC color register
  4127                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit color, in RGB order)
  4128                              <1> 	;		((EAX will return with color value))
  4129                              <1> 	;		CL = DAC color register (index)
  4130                              <1> 	;	   BL = 3 : Set/Write single DAC color register
  4131                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit color, in RGB order, bit 6&7 are 0)
  4132                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 0 - DAC color register
  4133                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 1 - Red (6 bit)
  4134                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 2 - Green (6 bit)
  4135                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 3 - Blue (6 bit)
  4136                              <1> 	;	   (BL>3 Alternative method for BMP files etc.)
  4137                              <1> 	;	   BL = 4 : Read all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4138                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit colors, in BGR order, bit 0&1 is 0)
  4139                              <1> 	;	   BL = 5 : Set all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4140                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit colors, in BGR order, bit 0&1 is 0)
  4141                              <1> 	;	   BL = 6 : Read single DAC color register
  4142                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit color, in BGR order, bit 0&1 is 0)
  4143                              <1> 	;		((EAX will return with color value))
  4144                              <1> 	;		CL = DAC color register (index)
  4145                              <1> 	;	   BL = 7 : Set/Write single DAC color register
  4146                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit color, bit 0&1 are 0)
  4147                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 0 - DAC color register
  4148                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 1 - Blue (8 bit)
  4149                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 2 - Green (8 bit)
  4150                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 3 - Red (8 bit)
  4151                              <1> 	;
  4152                              <1> 	;	  BL > 7 : invalid (not implemented)
  4153                              <1> 	;
  4154                              <1> 	;   if BL bit 2 is 1, 6 bit colors converted to 8 bit colors
  4155                              <1> 	;	(low two bits of color bytes will be 0)
  4156                              <1> 	;     ((color byte 00111111b will be converted to 11111100b))
  4157                              <1> 	;	and RGB byte order will be
  4158                              <1> 	;		byte 0 - Blue (low 2 bits are 0)
  4159                              <1> 	;		byte 1 - Green (low 2 bits are 0)
  4160                              <1> 	;		byte 2 - Red (low 2 bits are 0)
  4161                              <1> 	;		byte 3 - pad (or zero byte)
  4162                              <1> 	;	and 256 colors buffer size must be 256*4 = 1024 bytes
  4163                              <1> 	;   if BL bit 2 is 0, 6 bit colors will be used directly
  4164                              <1> 	;	  (high two bits of 8 bit color bytes will be 0)
  4165                              <1> 	;     ((dac color 111111b will be converted to 00111111b))
  4166                              <1> 	;		byte 0 - Red (high 2 bits are 0)
  4167                              <1> 	;		byte 1 - Green (high 2 bits are 0)
  4168                              <1> 	;		byte 2 - Blue (high 2 bits are 0)
  4169                              <1> 	;	and 256 colors buffer size must be 256*3 = 768 bytes
  4170                              <1> 	;
  4171                              <1> 	;	ECX = User's buffer addr (256*3 = 768 bytes) or
  4172                              <1> 	;	      Color
  4173                              <1> 	;
  4174                              <1> 	; Return:
  4175                              <1>         ;	EAX = buffer size (for BL input = 0,1,4,5)
  4176                              <1> 	;	      or color value (for BL input = 2,3,6,7)

  6618                              <1> pix_op_blk:
  6619                              <1> 	; 11/08/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
  6620                              <1> 	; 23/01/2021
  6621                              <1> 	; 22/02/2021
  6622                              <1> 	; 02/02/2021
  6623                              <1> 	; COPY PIXEL BLOCK -system to system-
  6624                              <1> 	; WRITE PIXEL BLOCKS -user to system-
  6625                              <1> 	;
  6626                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  6627                              <1> 	;   -If BL bit 5 is 0-
  6628                              <1> 	;    ECX = start position (row, column) (*)
  6629                              <1> 	;    (HW = row, CX = column)
  6630                              <1> 	;    EDX = size (rows, colums) (*)
  6631                              <1> 	;    (HW = rows, DX = columns)
  6632                              <1> 	;         (0 -> invalid)
  6633                              <1> 	;         (1 -> horizontal or vertical line)
  6634                              <1> 	;    ESI = destination (row, column) (***)
  6635                              <1> 	;   -If BL bit 5 is 1-	
  6636                              <1> 	;     CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  6637                              <1> 	;    ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  6638                              <1> 	;    EDX = count of blocks (not bytes)
  6639                              <1> 	;	 (limit: 2048 blocks/windows)
  6640                              <1> 	;    ESI = user's buffer address 
  6641                              <1> 	;	  contains 64 bit block data
  6642                              <1> 	;	  BLOCK ADDRESS - (row, col), dword
  6643                              <1> 	;	  (first 32 bits)
  6644                              <1> 	;	  BLOCK SIZE - (rows, cols), dword
  6645                              <1> 	;	  (second 32 bits)
  6646                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  6647                              <1> 	; 	[u.r0] will be > 0 if succesful
  6648                              <1> 
  6649                              <1> 	; Window option ([v_ops] bit 4) will be ignored
  6650                              <1> 	; (Function is used for display page coordinates)
  6651                              <1> 
  6652 0000F921 F605[ACBD0100]20    <1> 	test	byte [v_ops], 20h ; masked or direct ?

  6663 0000F944 E8C6F6FFFF          <1> 	call	calc_pixel_offset
  6664                              <1> 	; 22/02/2021

  6755                              <1> 	;   -If BL bit 5 is 0-	
  6756                              <1> 	;     CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  6757                              <1> 	;    ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  6758                              <1> 	;     DX = low 12 bits - size (length)
  6759                              <1> 	;	   high 4 bits - direction or type
  6760                              <1> 	;	     0 - Horizontal line
  6761                              <1> 	;	     1 - Vertical line
  6762                              <1> 	;	   > 1 - undefined, invalid
  6763                              <1> 	;    ESI = start position (row, column)
  6764                              <1> 	;	  (HW = row, SI = column)
  6765                              <1> 	;   -If BL bit 5 is 1-
  6766                              <1> 	;     CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  6767                              <1> 	;    ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  6768                              <1> 	;     DX = number of lines (in user buffer)
  6769                              <1> 	;	   (limit: 2048 lines)	
  6770                              <1> 	;    ESI = user's buffer
  6771                              <1> 	;          contains 64 bit data for lines
  6772                              <1> 	;	   START POINT: 32 bit (row, col)
  6773                              <1> 	;	   LENGTH: 32 bit
  6774                              <1> 	;		   high 16 bits - 0
  6775                              <1> 	;		   bit 0-11 - length
  6776                              <1> 	;	   	   bit 12-15 - type (length)
  6777                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  6778                              <1> 	; 	[u.r0] will be > 0 if succesful
  6779                              <1> 
  6780                              <1> 	; Window option ([v_ops] bit 4) will be ignored

  7746                              <1> pix_op_chr:
  7747                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
  7748                              <1> 	; 15/02/2021
  7749                              <1> 	; 05/02/2021
  7750                              <1> 	; WRITE CHARACTER (FONT)
  7751                              <1> 	; 05/01/2021 ([ufont])
  7752                              <1> 	; 01/01/2021
  7753                              <1> 	;     CL = char's color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  7754                              <1> 	;    ECX = char's color (16 bit and true colors)
  7755                              <1> 	;     DL = Character's ASCII code
  7756                              <1> 	;     DH bit 0 -> font height
  7757                              <1> 	;	  0 -> 8x16 character font
  7758                              <1> 	;	  1 -> 8x8 character font
  7759                              <1> 	;     DH bit 1 & 2 -> scale
  7760                              <1> 	;	  0 = 1/1 (8 pixels per char row)
  7761                              <1> 	;	  1 = 2/1 (16 pixels per char row)
  7762                              <1> 	;	  2 = 3/1 (24 pixels per char row)
  7763                              <1> 	;	  3 = 4/1 (32 pixels per char row)
  7764                              <1> 	;     DH bit 6 -> [ufont] option (1 = use [ufont])
  7765                              <1> 	;     If DH bit 7 = 1
  7766                              <1> 	;	 USER FONT (from user buffer)
  7767                              <1> 	;	    DL = 0 -> 8x8 (width: 1 byte per row)
  7768                              <1> 	;	    DL = 1 -> 8x16
  7769                              <1> 	;	    DL = 2 -> 16x16 (width: 2 bytes)
  7770                              <1> 	;	    DL = 3 -> 16x32
  7771                              <1> 	;	    DL = 4 -> 24x24 (width: 3 bytes)
  7772                              <1> 	;	    DL = 5 -> 24x48
  7773                              <1> 	;	    DL = 6 -> 32x32 (width: 4 bytes)
  7774                              <1> 	;	    DL = 7 -> 32x64
  7775                              <1> 	;	    DL > 7 -> invalid (unused)
  7776                              <1> 	;	 EDI = user's font buffer address
  7777                              <1> 	;	    (NOTE: byte order is as row0,row1,row2..)
  7778                              <1> 	;     ESI = start position (row, column) (*)
  7779                              <1> 	;	     (HW = row, SI = column)
  7780                              <1> 
  7781 0000FDB2 89F0                <1> 	mov	eax, esi ; start position
  7782 0000FDB4 E856F2FFFF          <1> 	call	calc_pixel_offset
  7783 0000FDB9 3B05[B2BD0100]      <1> 	cmp	eax, [v_siz]
  7784 0000FDBF 736D                <1> 	jnb	short pix_op_chr_err ; out of display page!
  7785 0000FDC1 E826F2FFFF          <1> 	call	pixels_to_byte_count
  7786                              <1> 	; eax = font start offset
  7787 0000FDC6 0305[AEBD0100]      <1> 	add	eax, [v_mem] ; LFB start address
  7788 0000FDCC A3[B6BD0100]        <1> 	mov	[v_str], eax ; font start address
  7789                              <1> 
  7790 0000FDD1 890D[BEBD0100]      <1> 	mov	[maskcolor], ecx ; save char's color
  7791                              <1> 
  7792 0000FDD7 8835[ACBD0100]      <1> 	mov	[v_ops], dh
  7793                              <1> 
  7794 0000FDDD 81E6FFFF0000        <1> 	and	esi, 0FFFFh
  7795 0000FDE3 8935[C6BD0100]      <1> 	mov	[buffer8], esi ; start column
  7796                              <1> 
  7797 0000FDE9 31DB                <1> 	xor	ebx, ebx ; 0
  7798 0000FDEB 31C0                <1> 	xor	eax, eax ; 15/02/2021
  7799                              <1> 
  7800 0000FDED F6C680              <1> 	test	dh, 80h
  7801 0000FDF0 7577                <1> 	jnz	short pix_op_chr_u ; user font
  7802                              <1> 
  7803 0000FDF2 80E63F              <1> 	and	dh, 3Fh ; clear bit 6, [UFONT] option bit
  7804 0000FDF5 7409                <1> 	jz	short pix_op_chr_0
  7805                              <1> 
  7806 0000FDF7 80FE07              <1> 	cmp	dh, 7
  7807 0000FDFA 7732                <1> 	ja	short pix_op_chr_err
  7808                              <1> 			 ; invalid (undefined) option
  7809 0000FDFC 88F4                <1> 	mov	ah, dh
  7810 0000FDFE D0EC                <1> 	shr	ah, 1
  7811                              <1> 	; ah = 0 to 3, scale
  7812                              <1> 	;jmp	short pix_op_chr_font_pixels
  7813                              <1> 
  7814                              <1> pix_op_chr_font_pixels:
  7815                              <1> 	; 05/02/2021
  7816                              <1> 	; write scaled font to buffer
  7817                              <1> 
  7818                              <1> 	; DL = ASCII code of character
  7819                              <1> 	; AH = scale

 12070                              <1> sysexec:
 12071                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0 
 12072                              <1> 	; 13/07/2026
 12073                              <1> 	; 12/07/2026
 12074                              <1> 	; 11/07/2026
 12075                              <1> 	; 10/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.11
 12076                              <1> 	; 07/07/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10 ; (v2.1.0)
 12077                              <1> 	; 21/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
 12078                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 12079                              <1> 	; 06/02/2022 - Retro UNIX 386 v1.2
 12080                              <1> 	; 18/11/2017
 12081                              <1> 	; 14/11/2017
 12082                              <1> 	; 13/11/2017
 12083                              <1> 	; 24/10/2016 - 04/01/2017
 12084                              <1> 	; 24/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 12085                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015 - 23/10/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 12086                              <1> 	; 03/06/2013 - 06/12/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 12087                              <1> 	;
 12088                              <1> 	; 'sysexec' initiates execution of a file whose path name if
 12089                              <1> 	; pointed to by 'name' in the sysexec call.
 12090                              <1> 	; 'sysexec' performs the following operations:
 12091                              <1> 	;    1. obtains i-number of file to be executed via 'namei'.
 12092                              <1> 	;    2. obtains i-node of file to be exceuted via 'iget'.
 12093                              <1> 	;    3. sets trap vectors to system routines.
 12094                              <1> 	;    4. loads arguments to be passed to executing file into
 12095                              <1> 	;	highest locations of user's core
 12096                              <1> 	;    5. puts pointers to arguments in locations immediately
 12097                              <1> 	;	following arguments.
 12098                              <1> 	;    6.	saves number of arguments in next location.
 12099                              <1> 	;    7. initializes user's stack area so that all registers
 12100                              <1> 	;	will be zeroed and the PS is cleared and the PC set
 12101                              <1> 	;	to core when 'sysret' restores registers
 12102                              <1> 	;	and does an rti.
 12103                              <1> 	;    8. initializes u.r0 and u.sp
 12104                              <1> 	;    9. zeros user's core down to u.r0
 12105                              <1> 	;   10.	reads executable file from storage device into core
 12106                              <1> 	;	starting at location 'core'.
 12107                              <1> 	;   11.	sets u.break to point to end of user's code with
 12108                              <1> 	;	data area appended.
 12109                              <1> 	;   12.	calls 'sysret' which returns control at location
 12110                              <1> 	;	'core' via 'rti' instruction.
 12111                              <1> 	;
 12112                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 12113                              <1> 	;	sysexec; namep; argp
 12114                              <1> 	; Arguments:
 12115                              <1> 	;	namep - points to pathname of file to be executed
 12116                              <1> 	;	argp  - address of table of argument pointers
 12117                              <1> 	;	argp1... argpn - table of argument pointers
 12118                              <1> 	;	argp1:<...0> ... argpn:<...0> - argument strings
 12119                              <1> 	; Inputs: (arguments)
 12120                              <1> 	; Outputs: -
 12121                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 12122                              <1> 	;
 12123                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification:
 12124                              <1> 	;	User application runs in it's own virtual space
 12125                              <1> 	;	which is izolated from kernel memory (and other
 12126                              <1> 	;	memory pages) via 80386	paging in ring 3
 12127                              <1> 	;	privilige mode. Virtual start address is always 0.
 12128                              <1> 	;	User's core memory starts at linear address 400000h
 12129                              <1> 	;	(the end of the 1st 4MB).
 12130                              <1> 	;
 12131                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
 12132                              <1> 	;	user/application segment and system/kernel segment
 12133                              <1> 	;	are different and sysenter/sysret/sysrele routines
 12134                              <1> 	;	are different (user's registers are saved to
 12135                              <1> 	;	and then restored from system's stack.)
 12136                              <1> 	;
 12137                              <1> 	;	NOTE: Retro UNIX 8086 v1 'arg2' routine gets these
 12138                              <1> 	;	      arguments which were in these registers;
 12139                              <1> 	;	      but, it returns by putting the 1st argument
 12140                              <1> 	;	      in 'u.namep' and the 2nd argument
 12141                              <1> 	;	      on top of stack. (1st argument is offset of the
 12142                              <1> 	;	      file/path name in the user's program segment.)
 12143                              <1> 
 12144                              <1> 	;call	arg2
 12145                              <1> 	; * name - 'u.namep' points to address of file/path name
 12146                              <1> 	;          in the user's program segment ('u.segmnt')
 12147                              <1> 	;          with offset in BX register (as sysopen argument 1).
 12148                              <1> 	; * argp - sysexec argument 2 is in CX register 
 12149                              <1> 	;          which is on top of stack.
 12150                              <1> 	;
 12151                              <1> 		; jsr r0,arg2 / arg0 in u.namep,arg1 on top of stack
 12152                              <1> 
 12153                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015 (32 bit modifications)
 12154                              <1> 
 12155                              <1> 	;; 13/11/2017

 12852                              <1> fclose:
 12853                              <1> 	; 16/01/2026
 12854                              <1> 	; 02/01/2026
 12855                              <1> 	; 24/04/2025
 12856                              <1> 	; 21/04/2025 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10 (v2.1 pre-work)
 12857                              <1> 	; 18/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9
 12858                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
 12859                              <1> 	; 06/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 12860                              <1> 	;
 12861                              <1> 	; 18/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 12862                              <1> 	;            (32 bit offset pointer modification)
 12863                              <1> 	; 19/04/2013 - 12/01/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 12864                              <1> 	;
 12865                              <1> 	; Given the file descriptor (index to the u.fp list)
 12866                              <1> 	; 'fclose' first gets the i-number of the file via 'getf'.
 12867                              <1> 	; If i-node is active (i-number > 0) the entry in
 12868                              <1> 	; u.fp list is cleared. If all the processes that opened
 12869                              <1> 	; that file close it, then fsp entry is freed and the file
 12870                              <1> 	; is closed. If not a return is taken.
 12871                              <1> 	; If the file has been deleted while open, 'anyi' is called

 13107                              <1> sysbreak:
 13108                              <1> 	; 06/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
 13109                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 13110                              <1> 	; 18/10/2015
 13111                              <1> 	; 07/10/2015
 13112                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13113                              <1> 	; 20/06/2013 - 24/03/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13114                              <1> 	;
 13115                              <1> 	; 'sysbreak' sets the programs break points.
 13116                              <1> 	; It checks the current break point (u.break) to see if it is
 13117                              <1> 	; between "core" and the stack (sp). If it is, it is made an
 13118                              <1> 	; even address (if it was odd) and the area between u.break
 13119                              <1> 	; and the stack is cleared. The new breakpoint is then put
 13120                              <1> 	; in u.break and control is passed to 'sysret'.
 13121                              <1> 	;
 13122                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 13123                              <1> 	;	sysbreak; addr
 13124                              <1> 	; Arguments: -
 13125                              <1> 	;
 13126                              <1> 	; Inputs: u.break - current breakpoint
 13127                              <1> 	; Outputs: u.break - new breakpoint 
 13128                              <1> 	;	area between old u.break and the stack (sp) is cleared.
 13129                              <1> 	;
 13130                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 13131                              <1> 	; 06/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9 - Major Modification -
 13132                              <1> 	;
 13133                              <1> 	; 	This system call performs "malloc" function as in C.
 13134                              <1> 	; Input:
 13135                              <1> 	;    EBX = new u.break address (virtual, user's space)
 13136                              <1> 	; (Note: Default/Initial u.break address is the start of the BSS
 13137                              <1> 	;	 section. Or it is file size for PRG -flat image- files.)
 13138                              <1> 	; If EBX = 0FFFFFFFFh ; -1
 13139                              <1> 	;    Return current u.break in EAX
 13140                              <1> 	; Output:
 13141                              <1> 	;    If EBX input is -1, EAX = current u.break address (virtual)
 13142                              <1> 	;	otherwise, EAX = new u.break address
 13143                              <1> 	; Area between the new u.break and the old u.break is cleared.
 13144                              <1> 	; (Note: If the new break address cross overs user's esp,
 13145                              <1> 	;	 this area <new break - old break> is not cleared.)
 13146                              <1> 	; If CF=1 at return, it means Memory Allocation Error.
 13147                              <1> 	;		(or "Insufficient Memory" error)
 13148                              <1> 	;	EAX = 0
 13149                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 13150                              <1> 	;
 13151                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
 13152                              <1> 	;	The user/application program puts breakpoint address
 13153                              <1> 	;       in BX register as 'sysbreak' system call argument.
 13154                              <1> 	; 	(argument transfer method 1)
 13155                              <1> 	;
 13156                              <1> 	;  NOTE: Beginning of core is 0 in Retro UNIX 8086 v1 !
 13157                              <1> 	; 	((!'sysbreak' is not needed in Retro UNIX 8086 v1!))
 13158                              <1> 	;  NOTE:
 13159                              <1> 	; 	'sysbreak' clears extended part (beyond of previous
 13160                              <1> 	;	'u.break' address) of user's memory for original unix's
 13161                              <1> 	;	'bss' compatibility with Retro UNIX 8086 v1 (19/11/2013)
 13162                              <1> 
 13163                              <1> 		; mov u.break,r1 / move users break point to r1
 13164                              <1> 		; cmp r1,$core / is it the same or lower than core?
 13165                              <1> 		; blos 1f / yes, 1f
 13166                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015

 13257                              <1> sysseek: ; / moves read write pointer in an fsp entry
 13258                              <1> 	; 27/12/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
 13259                              <1> 	; 06/11/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 13260                              <1> 	; 22/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13261                              <1> 	; 07/07/2013 - 05/08/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13262                              <1> 	;
 13263                              <1> 	; 'sysseek' changes the r/w pointer of (3rd word of in an
 13264                              <1> 	; fsp entry) of an open file whose file descriptor is in u.r0.
 13265                              <1> 	; The file descriptor refers to a file open for reading or
 13266                              <1> 	; writing. The read (or write) pointer is set as follows:
 13267                              <1> 	;	* if 'ptrname' is 0, the pointer is set to offset.
 13268                              <1> 	;	* if 'ptrname' is 1, the pointer is set to its
 13269                              <1> 	;	  current location plus offset.
 13270                              <1> 	;	* if 'ptrname' is 2, the pointer is set to the
 13271                              <1> 	;	  size of file plus offset.
 13272                              <1> 	; The error bit (e-bit) is set for an undefined descriptor.
 13273                              <1> 	;
 13274                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 13275                              <1> 	;	sysseek; offset; ptrname
 13276                              <1> 	; Arguments:
 13277                              <1> 	;	offset - number of bytes desired to move
 13278                              <1> 	;		 the r/w pointer
 13279                              <1> 	;	ptrname - a switch indicated above
 13280                              <1> 	;
 13281                              <1> 	; Inputs: r0 - file descriptor
 13282                              <1> 	;	; 27/12/2025
 13283                              <1> 	;	EBX = File descriptor (number) -user-
 13284                              <1> 	;	ECX = Offset (plus)
 13285                              <1> 	;	EDX = 0 -> set to offset in ECX
 13286                              <1> 	;	    = 1 -> set to current offset + offset in ECX
 13287                              <1> 	;	    = 2 -> set to file size + offset in ECX
 13288                              <1> 	; Outputs: -
 13289                              <1> 	;	EAX = (new) File Offset ; 27/12/2025
 13290                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 13291                              <1> 	;
 13292                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
 13293                              <1> 	;       'sysseek' system call has three arguments; so,
 13294                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, file descriptor is in BX (BL) register
 13295                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, offset is in CX register
 13296                              <1> 	;	* 3rd argument, ptrname/switch is in DX (DL) register
 13297                              <1> 
 13298 00011B76 E823000000          <1> 	call	seektell
 13299                              <1> 	; EAX = Current R/W pointer of the file
 13300                              <1> 	; EBX = [u.fofp]
 13301                              <1> 	; [u.base] = offset (ECX input)
 13302                              <1>

 13412                              <1> sysintr: ; / set interrupt handling
 13413                              <1> 	; 21/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9 modification
 13414                              <1> 	; 22/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13415                              <1> 	; 07/07/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13416                              <1> 	;
 13417                              <1> 	; 'sysintr' sets the interrupt handling value. It puts
 13418                              <1> 	; argument of its call in u.intr then branches into 'sysquit'
 13419                              <1> 	; routine. u.tty is checked if to see if a control tty exists.
 13420                              <1> 	; If one does the interrupt character in the tty buffer is
 13421                              <1> 	; cleared and 'sysret'is called. If one does not exits
 13422                              <1> 	; 'sysret' is just called.
 13423                              <1> 	;
 13424                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 13425                              <1> 	;	sysintr; arg
 13426                              <1> 	; Argument:
 13427                              <1> 	;	arg - if 0, interrupts (ASCII DELETE) are ignored.
 13428                              <1> 	;	    - if 1, interrupts cause their normal result
 13429                              <1> 	;		 i.e force an exit.
 13430                              <1> 	;	    - if arg is a location within the program,
 13431                              <1> 	;		control is passed to that location when
 13432                              <1> 	;		an interrupt occurs.
 13433                              <1> 	; Inputs: -
 13434                              <1> 	; Outputs: -
 13435                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 13436                              <1> 	;
 13437                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
 13438                              <1> 	;       'sysintr' system call sets u.intr to value of BX
 13439                              <1> 	;	then branches into sysquit.
 13440                              <1> 
 13441                              <1> 	; 21/08/2024 - TRDOS 386
 13442                              <1> 	; enable/disable terminate (CTRL+BREAK) interrupt 
 13443                              <1> 	;
 13444                              <1> 	; INPUT:
 13445                              <1> 	;	bx = 0 -> disable CTRL+BREAK
 13446                              <1> 	;		-u.intr will be set to 0, u.quit will be ignored-
 13447                              <1> 	;	bx > 0 -> enable CTRL+BREAK (also default at start)
 13448                              <1> 	;		-u.intr will be set to 0FFFFh, u.quit will be used-
 13449                              <1> 	;	NOTE: u.quit is flag for CTRL+BREAK key press status
 13450                              <1> 	;	      -1 = pressed -termination request-, 0 = not pressed
 13451                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
 13452                              <1> 	;	none
 13453                              <1>

 13468                              <1> sysquit:
 13469                              <1> 	; 21/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9 modification
 13470                              <1> 	;	get/reset QUIT (u.quit) status
 13471                              <1> 	;
 13472                              <1> 	; 22/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13473                              <1> 	; 07/07/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13474                              <1> 	;
 13475                              <1> 	; 'sysquit' turns off the quit signal. it puts the argument of
 13476                              <1> 	; the call in u.quit. u.tty is checked if to see if a control

 13487                              <1> 	;		cease and a core image to be produced.

 13534                              <1> anyi: 
 13535                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022
 13536                              <1> 	; 06/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 13537                              <1> 	; Major Modification!
 13538                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 does not permit to delete a file while it is open
 13539                              <1> 	; The role of 'anyi' procedure has beeen changed to ensure that.
 13540                              <1> 	; 
 13541                              <1> 	; 22/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13542                              <1> 	; 25/04/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13543                              <1> 	;
 13544                              <1> 	; 'anyi' is called if a file deleted while open.
 13545                              <1> 	; "anyi" checks to see if someone else has opened this file.
 13546                              <1> 	;
 13547                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 13548                              <1> 	;    r1 - contains an i-number
 13549                              <1> 	;    fsp - start of table containing open files
 13550                              <1> 	;
 13551                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 13552                              <1> 	;    "deleted" flag set in fsp entry of another occurrence of
 13553                              <1> 	;	   this file and r2 points 1st word of this fsp entry.
 13554                              <1> 	;    if file not found - bit in i-node map is cleared
 13555                              <1> 	;    			 (i-node is freed)
 13556                              <1> 	;               all blocks related to i-node are freed
 13557                              <1> 	;	        all flags in i-node are cleared
 13558                              <1> 	; ((AX = R1)) input
 13559                              <1> 	;
 13560                              <1> 	;    (Retro UNIX Prototype : 02/12/2012, UNIXCOPY.ASM)
 13561                              <1>         ;    ((Modified registers: EDX, ECX, EBX, ESI, EDI, EBP))
 13562                              <1> 	;
 13563                              <1> 	; / r1 contains an i-number
 13564                              <1> 
 13565                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (06/10/2016)
 13566                              <1> 	; 
 13567                              <1> 	; INPUT:
 13568                              <1> 	;	EAX = First Cluster
 13569                              <1> 	;	 DL = Logical DOS Drive Number
 13570                              <1> 	;
 13571                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
 13572                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 -> EBX = File Handle/Number/Index
 13573                              <1> 	;	CF = 0 -> EBX = 0
 13574                              <1> 	;
 13575                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EBX
 13576                              <1> 
 13577                              <1> 	xor	ebx, ebx
 13578                              <1> anyi_0: 
 13579                              <1> 	cmp	byte [ebx+OF_MODE], 0 ; 0 = empty entry
 13580                              <1> 	ja	short anyi_2 ; 1 (r), 2 (w) or 3 (r&w)
 13581                              <1> anyi_1:
 13582                              <1> 	inc	bl
 13583                              <1> 	cmp	bl, OPENFILES ; max. count of open files
 13584                              <1> 	jb	short anyi_0
 13585                              <1> 	xor	eax, eax
 13586                              <1> 	retn
 13587                              <1> anyi_2:
 13588                              <1> 	cmp	dl, [ebx+OF_DRIVE]
 13589                              <1> 	jne	short anyi_1
 13590                              <1> 	;shl	bx, 2 ; *4 (dword offset)
 13591                              <1> 	shl	ebx, 2 ; 23/07/2022
 13592                              <1> 	cmp	eax, [ebx+OF_FCLUSTER]
 13593                              <1> 	je	short anyi_3
 13594                              <1> 	;shr	bx, 2 ; /4 (byte offset)
 13595                              <1> 	shr	ebx, 2 ; 23/07/2022
 13596                              <1> 	jmp	short anyi_1
 13597                              <1> anyi_3:
 13598                              <1> 	;shr	bx, 2 ; /4 (bytes offset) (index)
 13599                              <1> 	shr	ebx, 2 ; 23/07/2022
 13600                              <1> 	stc
 13601                              <1> 	retn

 14566                              <1> tswitch: ; Retro UNIX 386 v1
 14567                              <1> tswap:
 14568                              <1> 	; 16/01/2017
 14569                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 14570                              <1> 	; 10/05/2015 - 01/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 14571                              <1> 	; 14/04/2013 - 14/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14572                              <1> 	; time out swap, called when a user times out.
 14573                              <1> 	; the user is put on the low priority queue.
 14574                              <1> 	; This is done by making a link from the last user
 14575                              <1> 	; on the low priority queue to him via a call to 'putlu'.
 14576                              <1> 	; then he is swapped out.
 14577                              <1> 
 14578                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) modification ->  ** 21/05/2016 **
 14579                              <1> 	;     * when a high priority (event) process will be stopped
 14580                              <1> 	;	(swapped out, swithched out/off), 'tswap/tswitch' will
 14581                              <1> 	;	not add it to a run queue.
 14582                              <1> 	;	/// What for: Process may be already in a run queue, 
 14583                              <1> 	;	it is unspeficied state because process might be started
 14584                              <1> 	;	by a timer event which does not regard previous priority
 14585                              <1> 	;	level and run queue of the process (for fast executing!).
 14586                              <1> 	;	After the 'run for event', process will be sequenced
 14587                              <1> 	;	to run by it's actual run queue. ///
 14588                              <1> 	;
 14589                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification ->
 14590                              <1> 	;       swap (software task switch) is performed by changing
 14591                              <1> 	;	user's page directory (u.pgdir) instead of segment change
 14592                              <1> 	;	as in Retro UNIX 8086 v1.
 14593                              <1> 	;
 14594                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14595                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14596                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14597                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14598                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory
 14599                              <1> 	;	in 8086/8088 times.
 14600                              <1> 	;
 14601                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14602                              <1> 	;    u.uno - users process number
 14603                              <1> 	;    runq+4 - lowest priority queue
 14604                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 14605                              <1> 	;    r0 - users process number
 14606                              <1> 	;    r2 - lowest priority queue address
 14607                              <1> 	;
 14608                              <1> 	; ((AX = R0, BX = R2)) output
 14609                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI))
 14610                              <1> 	;
 14611                              <1> 
 14612                              <1> 	NOTE:
 14613                              <1> 	;* [u.pri] priority level is specified by run queue which is process
 14614                              <1> 	;  comes to run from.
 14615                              <1> 	;* Initial [u.pri] is 1 ('normal/regular') for programs
 14616                              <1> 	;  (which are launched by MainProg or 'sysexec'), it is changed
 14617                              <1> 	;  to 2 ('high') by timer event, if program uses 'systimer' system call.
 14618                              <1> 	;* Program (Process) also can change it's running priority
 14619                              <1> 	;  from 1 to 0 or up to 2 by using 'syspri' system call; but,
 14620                              <1> 	;  if program selects priority level 2 (high) for running, next time
 14621                              <1> 	;  it is reduced to 1 (normal/regular) because 'syspri' adds this
 14622                              <1> 	;  program to 'run for normal' queue while running duration is a bit
 14623                              <1> 	;  protected from swap/switch out immediate, behalf of other high
 14624                              <1> 	;  priority process in sequence. Program (with high priority) will not
 14625                              <1> 	;  be swapped/switched out (by timer event) before it's time quantum
 14626                              <1> 	;  will be elapsed, but, this will be temporary if program is not using
 14627                              <1> 	;  timer event function.
 14628                              <1> 
 14629                              <1> 	;For example:
 14630                              <1> 	;If a process frequently gets a timer event, it runs at high priority
 14631                              <1> 	;level but when it returns from running it returns to actual run queue,
 14632                              <1> 	;not to 'run for event' queue again.
 14633                              <1> 	;'tswap' will not change the sequence at return/stop(swap out) stage.
 14634                              <1> 	;But if priority level not high (=2, 'run for event'), 'tswap/tswitch'
 14635                              <1> 	;will add the stopping process to relevant run queue according to
 14636                              <1> 	;[u.pri] priority level.
 14637                              <1> 
 14638                              <1> 	; 16/01/2017
 14639 00012114 BB[06B00100]        <1> 	mov	ebx, runq+2 	; 'runq_normal' ; normal/regular priority
 14640                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016
 14641                              <1> 	;cmp	byte [u.pri], 2	; high priority (run for event) ?
 14642                              <1> 	;jnb	short swap
 14643                              <1> 	; 16/01/2017
 14644                              <1> 	; (Normal and also high/event priority processes will be added to
 14645                              <1> 	; normal priority run queue for ensuring circular running sequence!)
 14646                              <1> 	; (Timer interrupt or 'syspri' system call may change priority and run
 14647                              <1> 	; queue to high/event level.)
 14648 00012119 803D[41B00100]00    <1> 	cmp	byte [u.pri], 0

 14650                              <1> 	;

 14674                              <1> 	; 'swap' is routine that controls the swapping of processes
 14675                              <1> 	; in and out of core.
 14676                              <1> 	;
 14677                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) modification ->  ** 20/05/2016 **
 14678                              <1> 	;     * 3 different priority level is applied
 14679                              <1> 	;	(just as original unix v1)
 14680                              <1> 	;	1) high priority (event) run queue, 'runq_event'
 14681                              <1> 	;	2) normal priority (regular) run queue, 'runq_normal'
 14682                              <1> 	;	3) low priority (background) run queue, 'runq_backgroud'
 14683                              <1> 	;	'swap' code will run a process which has max. priority
 14684                              <1>         ;       (for earliest event at first)
 14685                              <1> 	;
 14686                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification ->
 14687                              <1> 	;       swap (software task switch) is performed by changing
 14688                              <1> 	;	user's page directory (u.pgdir) instead of segment change
 14689                              <1> 	;	as in Retro UNIX 8086 v1.
 14690                              <1> 	;
 14691                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14692                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14693                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14694                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14695                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory
 14696                              <1> 	;	in 8086/8088 times.
 14697                              <1> 	;
 14698                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14699                              <1> 	;    runq table - contains processes to run.
 14700                              <1> 	;    p.link - contains next process in line to be run.
 14701                              <1> 	;    u.uno - process number of process in core
 14702                              <1> 	;    s.stack - swap stack used as an internal stack for swapping.
 14703                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 14704                              <1> 	;    (original unix v1 -> present process to its disk block)
 14705                              <1> 	;    (original unix v1 -> new process into core -> 
 14706                              <1> 	;	   Retro Unix 8086 v1 -> segment registers changed
 14707                              <1> 	;	   for new process)
 14708                              <1> 	;    u.quant = 3 (Time quantum for a process)
 14709                              <1> 	; 	((INT 1Ch count down speed -> 18.2 times per second)
 14710                              <1> 	;    RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 will use INT 1Ch (18.2 times per second)
 14711                              <1> 	;	 for now, it will swap the process if there is not
 14712                              <1> 	;	 a keyboard event (keystroke) (Int 15h, function 4Fh)
 14713                              <1> 	;	 or will count down from 3 to 0 even if there is a
 14714                              <1> 	;        keyboard event locking due to repetitive key strokes.
 14715                              <1> 	;	 u.quant will be reset to 3 for RETRO UNIX 8086 v1.
 14716                              <1> 	;
 14717                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EAX, EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI))
 14718                              <1> 
 14719                              <1> 	;NOTE:
 14720                              <1> 	;High priority queue is the first for selecting a process to run.
 14721                              <1> 	;If there is not a process in high priority level run queue,
 14722                              <1> 	;a process in normal priority run queue will be selected
 14723                              <1> 	;or a proces in low priority run queue will be selected if normal
 14724                              <1> 	;priority level run queue is empty.

 14800                              <1> wswap:  ; < swap out, swap to disk >
 14801                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017 (fnsave)
 14802                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 14803                              <1> 	; 09/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 14804                              <1> 	; 26/05/2013 - 08/03/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14805                              <1> 	; 'wswap' writes out the process that is in core onto its
 14806                              <1> 	; appropriate disk area.
 14807                              <1> 	;
 14808                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification ->
 14809                              <1> 	;       User (u) structure content and the user's register content
 14810                              <1> 	;	will be copied to the process's/user's UPAGE (a page for
 14811                              <1> 	;	saving 'u' structure and user registers for task switching).
 14812                              <1> 	;	u.usp - points to kernel stack address which contains
 14813                              <1> 	;		user's registers while entering system call.
 14814                              <1> 	;	u.sp  - points to kernel stack address
 14815                              <1> 	;		to return from system call -for IRET-.
 14816                              <1> 	;	[u.usp]+32+16 = [u.sp] 
 14817                              <1> 	;	[u.usp] -> edi, esi, ebp, esp (= [u.usp]+32), ebx,
 14818                              <1> 	;		edx, ecx, eax, gs, fs, es, ds, -> [u.sp].
 14819                              <1> 	;
 14820                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14821                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14822                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14823                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14824                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory 
 14825                              <1> 	;	in 8086/8088 times.
 14826                              <1> 	;
 14827                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14828                              <1> 	;    u.break - points to end of program

 14830                              <1> 	;    core - beginning of process program
 14831                              <1> 	;    ecore - end of core
 14832                              <1> 	;    user - start of user parameter area
 14833                              <1> 	;    u.uno - user process number
 14834                              <1> 	;    p.dska - holds block number of process

 14836                              <1> 	;    swp I/O queue
 14837                              <1> 	;    p.break - negative word count of process

 14879                              <1> rswap:  ; < swap in, swap from disk >
 14880                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017 (frstor)

 14893                              <1> 	;	will be restored from process's/user's UPAGE (a page for

 14895                              <1> 	;	u.usp - points to kernel stack address which contains
 14896                              <1> 	;		user's registers while entering system call.
 14897                              <1> 	;	u.sp  - points to kernel stack address
 14898                              <1> 	;		to return from system call -for IRET-.
 14899                              <1> 	;	[u.usp]+32+16 = [u.sp]

 14901                              <1> 	;		edx, ecx, eax, gs, fs, es, ds, -> [u.sp].
 14902                              <1> 	;
 14903                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14904                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14905                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14906                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14907                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory

 14974                              <1> 	; 15/04/2013 - 23/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14975                              <1> 	; 'putlu' is called with a process number in r1 and a pointer
 14976                              <1> 	; to lowest priority Q (runq+4) in r2. A link is created from
 14977                              <1> 	; the last process on the queue to process in r1 by putting
 14978                              <1> 	; the process number in r1 into the last process's link.
 14979                              <1> 	;

 14981                              <1> 	;    r1 - user process number
 14982                              <1> 	;    r2 - points to lowest priority queue
 14983                              <1> 	;    p.dska - disk address of the process
 14984                              <1> 	;    u.emt - determines handling of emt's
 14985                              <1> 	;    u.ilgins - determines handling of illegal instructions

 14988                              <1> 	;	  entering putlu

 14990                              <1> 	;    r2 - points to lowest priority queue

 14993                              <1> 	;

 15003                              <1> 		; which is one of following addresses:

 15042                              <1> syspri: ; change running priority (of the process)
 15043                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 15044                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016
 15045                              <1> 	; 20/05/2026 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 15046                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 15047                              <1> 	;	BL = priority level
 15048                              <1> 	;	   0 = low running priority (running on background)
 15049                              <1> 	;	   1 = normal/regular priority (running as regular)
 15050                              <1> 	;	   2 = high/event priority (running for event)
 15051                              <1> 	;	   >2 = invalid, it will accepted as 2 (event)
 15052                              <1> 	;	   0FFh = get/return current running priority only
 15053                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 15054                              <1> 	;	* if current [u.pri] < 2
 15055                              <1> 	;	  if BL input < 0FFh ->
 15056                              <1> 	;	     [u.pri] is updated as in BL input (0,1,2)
 15057                              <1> 	;	  if BL input = 0FFh -> AL = [u.pri] (current)
 15058                              <1> 	;
 15059                              <1> 	;	* if current [u.pri] = 2
 15060                              <1> 	;	  if BL input < 0FFh -> cf = 1 & AL = 2
 15061                              <1> 	;	  if BL input = 0FFh -> cf = 0 & AL = 2
 15062                              <1> 	;
 15063                              <1> 	;	NOTE:
 15064                              <1> 	;	If [u.pri] = 2, it can not be changed to 1 or 0;
 15065                              <1> 	;	because, run queue of the running process is unspecified
 15066                              <1> 	;	at this	stage. Process might be started by a timer event
 15067                              <1> 	;	or priority might be changed to high by previous
 15068                              <1> 	;	'syspri' system	call. In both cases, the process is in
 15069                              <1> 	;	'runq_normal' or 'runq_background' queue.
 15070                              <1> 	;	As result of this fact, when the [u.quant] time quantum
 15071                              <1> 	;	of the process is elapsed or 'sysrele' system call is
 15072                              <1> 	;	instructed by the process, 'tswap' ('tswitch') procedure
 15073                              <1> 	;	will be called (to 'swap' or 'switch' out the procedure)
 15074                              <1> 	;	and it will not call 'putlu' to add the (stopping)
 15075                              <1> 	;	process to relevant run queue when [u.pri] = 2.
 15076                              <1> 	;	(Otherwise, it would be possible to add process to
 15077                              <1> 	;	a run queue while it is already in a run queue, wrongly.)
 15078                              <1>   	;
 15079                              <1> 	;	If [u.pri]< 2, 'tswap/tswitch' procedure will call
 15080                              <1> 	;	'putlu' to add process to relevant run queue
 15081                              <1> 	;	according to [u.pri] value. ('runq_normal' for 1,
 15082                              <1> 	;	'runq_background' for 0).
 15083                              <1> 	;
 15084                              <1> 	;	If BL input >= 2 and < 0FFh while [u.pri] < 2,
 15085                              <1> 	;	process will be added to 'runq_normal' queue and
 15086                              <1> 	;	[u.pri] will be set to 2. (in 'syspri' system call)
 15087                              <1> 	;
 15088                              <1> 
 15089 0001225A 29C0                <1> 	sub	eax, eax ; 0
 15090 0001225C A3[64B00100]        <1> 	mov	[u.error], eax
 15091                              <1>

 15093 00012266 A3[14B00100]        <1> 	mov	[u.r0], eax
 15094                              <1> 
 15095 0001226B FEC3                <1> 	inc	bl
 15096                              <1> 	;jz	sysret ; 0FFh -> 0, get priority level
 15097                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022
 15098 0001226D 742C                <1> 	jz	short syspri_2	; jmp sysret
 15099                              <1> 
 15100 0001226F 3C02                <1> 	cmp	al, 2
 15101                              <1> 	;jnb	error ; CF = 1 & AL = 2 (& last error = 0)
 15102                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022
 15103 00012271 7205                <1> 	jb	short syspri_0
 15104 00012273 E99FBEFFFF          <1> 	jmp	error
 15105                              <1> syspri_0:
 15106 00012278 FECB                <1> 	dec	bl
 15107 0001227A 80FB02              <1> 	cmp	bl, 2

 15119                              <1> 	; ('run for event') but current process will be added to
 15120                              <1> 	; 'run as normal' queue. ('run for event' high priority

 15124                              <1> 	; e.g. if it is not in waiting list and it has not got

 15126                              <1> 	; Because, when [u.pri] is 2, 'tswap/tswitch' will not
