 15331                              <1> sysfff: ; <Find First File>
 15332                              <1> 	; 25/05/2025
 15333                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10) ((v2.1.0))
 15334                              <1> 	; 25/08/2024 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9)
 15335                              <1> 	; 08/08/2022
 15336                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
 15337                              <1> 	; 17/10/2016
 15338                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016
 15339                              <1> 	; 15/10/2016 TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) feature only !
 15340                              <1> 	;           -derived from TRDOS v1.0, INT_21H.ASM-
 15341                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_find_first_file")
 15342                              <1> 	; TRDOS 8086 (v1.0)
 15343                              <1>         ; 	07/08/2011
 15344                              <1>         ;	Find First File
 15345                              <1> 	;	INPUT:
 15346                              <1>         ;	    CX= Attributes
 15347                              <1>         ;	    DS:DX= Pointer to filename
 15348                              <1> 	;	MSDOS OUTPUT:
 15349                              <1> 	;	    DTA: (Default address: PSP offset 80h)
 15350                              <1> 	;	    Offset  Descrription
 15351                              <1> 	;	    0	    Reserved for use find next file
 15352                              <1> 	;	    21	    Attribute of file found
 15353                              <1> 	;	    22	    Time stamp of file
 15354                              <1> 	;	    24	    Date stamp of file
 15355                              <1> 	;	    26	    File size in bytes
 15356                              <1> 	;	    30	    Filename and extension (zero terminated)
 15357                              <1> 	;	If cf = 1:
 15358                              <1> 	;	    Error Codes: (in AX)
 15359                              <1> 	;	    	2 - File not found
 15360                              <1> 	;	       18 - No more files
 15361                              <1>         ;
 15362                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (v2.0)
 15363                              <1> 	; 15/10/2016
 15364                              <1> 	;
 15365                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
 15366                              <1>         ;	   CL = File attributes
 15367                              <1> 	;     	      bit 0 (1) - Read only file (R)
 15368                              <1> 	;             bit 1 (1) - Hidden file (H)
 15369                              <1>         ;             bit 2 (1) - System file (R)
 15370                              <1> 	;             bit 3 (1) - Volume label/name (V)
 15371                              <1>         ;             bit 4 (1) - Subdirectory (D)
 15372                              <1> 	;	      bit 5 (1) - File has been archived (A)
 15373                              <1> 	;	   CH = 0 -> Return basic parameters (24 bytes)
 15374                              <1> 	;	   CH > 0 -> Return FindFile structure/table (128 bytes)
 15375                              <1>         ;          EBX = Pointer to filename (ASCIIZ) -path-
 15376                              <1> 	;	   EDX = File parameters buffer address
 15377                              <1> 	;		(buffer size = 24 bytes if CH input = 0)
 15378                              <1> 	;		(buffer size = 128 bytes if CH input > 0)
 15379                              <1> 	;
 15380                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 15381                              <1> 	;	   EAX = 0 if CH input > 0
 15382                              <1> 	;	   EAX = First cluster number of file if CH input = 0
 15383                              <1> 	;	   EDX = File parameters table/structure address
 15384                              <1> 	;	   Basic Parameters:
 15385                              <1> 	;		Offset  Description
 15386                              <1> 	;		------	---------------
 15387                              <1> 	;		0	File Attributes
 15388                              <1> 	;		1	Ambiguous filename chars are used sign
 15389                              <1> 	;			(0 = filename fits exactly with request)
 15390                              <1> 	;			(>0 = ambiguous filename chars are used)
 15391                              <1> 	;	      	2	Time stamp of file
 15392                              <1> 	;		4	Date stamp of file
 15393                              <1> 	;		6	File size in bytes
 15394                              <1> 	;		10	Short Filename (ASCIIZ, max. 13 bytes)
 15395                              <1> 	;		23	Longname Length (1-255) if existing
 15396                              <1> 	;
 15397                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
 15398                              <1> 	;
 15399                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
 15400                              <1> 	;
 15401                              <1> 	; TR-DOS FindFile (FFF) Structure (128 bytes):
 15402                              <1> 	; 09/10/2011 (DIR.ASM) - 10/02/2016 (trdoskx.s)
 15403                              <1> 	;
 15404                              <1> 	; Offset   Parameter			Size
 15405                              <1> 	; ------   ------------------		--------
 15406                              <1> 	; 0	   FindFile_Drv			1 byte
 15407                              <1> 	; 1	   FindFile_Directory		65 bytes
 15408                              <1> 	; 66	   FindFile_Name		13 bytes
 15409                              <1> 	; 79	   FindFile_LongNameEntryLength 1 byte
 15410                              <1> 	;Above 80 bytes form
 15411                              <1> 	;TR-DOS Source/Destination File FullName Format/Structure
 15412                              <1> 	; 80	   FindFile_AttributesMask	1 word
 15413                              <1> 	; 82	   FindFile_DirEntry		32 bytes (*)
 15414                              <1> 	; 114	   FindFile_DirFirstCluster	1 double word
 15415                              <1> 	; 118	   FindFile_DirCluster		1 double word
 15416                              <1> 	; 122	   FindFile_DirEntryNumber	1 word
 15417                              <1> 	; 124	   FindFile_MatchCounter	1 word
 15418                              <1> 	; 126	   FindFile_Reserved		1 word
 15419                              <1>    	; (*) MS-DOS, FAT 12-16-32 classic directory entry (32 bytes)
 15420                              <1> 	;
 15421                              <1> 	; ***********************************************************
 15422                              <1> 	;
 15423                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (Major Modification)
 15424                              <1> 	; ------ TR-DOS 386 v2.0.10 --------
 15425                              <1> 	; FindFile - SysFFF/SysFNF Structure (<=281 bytes):
 15426                              <1> 	;
 15427                              <1> 	; Offset   Parameter			Size
 15428                              <1> 	; ------   ------------------		--------
 15429                              <1> 	; 0	   FindFile_DirEntry		32 bytes (*)
 15430                              <1> 	; 32	   FindFile_Drv			1 byte
 15431                              <1> 	; 33	   FindFile_Directory		65 bytes (104 bytes)
 15432                              <1> 	; 98	   FindFile_Name		13 bytes
 15433                              <1> 	; 111	   FindFile_LongNameEntryLength 1 byte
 15434                              <1> 	; 112	   FindFile_Longname		129 bytes (max.) (**)
 15435                              <1> 	;
 15436                              <1> 	; Parameters table/structure size: max. 280 bytes (**)
 15437                              <1> 	;
 15438                              <1> 	;		; 25/05/2025 (**)
 15439                              <1> 	; Return Options:
 15440                              <1> 	;	CH = 0 -> basic (24 bytes)
 15441                              <1> 	;	CH bits
 15442                              <1> 	;	   bit 0 - FindFile_DirEntry
 15443                              <1> 	;	   bit 1 - FindFile_Drv
 15444                              <1> 	;	   bit 2 - FindFile_Directory (65 bytes)
 15445                              <1> 	;	   bit 3 - FindFile_Name
 15446                              <1> 	;	   bit 4 - FindFile_LongNameEntryLength
 15447                              <1> 	;	   bit 5 - FindFile_Longname (65 bytes) (ASCIIZ)
 15448                              <1> 	;	   bit 6 - use 104 bytes buf for directory
 15449                              <1> 	;	   bit 7 - use 128+1 bytes buf for longname (**)
 15450                              <1> 	; 	examples:
 15451                              <1> 	;	  1Fh -	00011111b needs 112 bytes buffer
 15452                              <1> 	;	  0Fh -	01001111b needs 150 bytes buffer
 15453                              <1> 	;	 0EFh -	11101111b needs 279 bytes buffer
 15454                              <1> 	;	 0FFh -	11111111b needs 280 bytes buffer (**)
 15455                              <1> 	;	 07Fh - 01111111b needs 216 bytes buffer (**)
 15456                              <1> 	;	 03Fh - 00111111b needs 177 bytes buffer (**)
 15457                              <1> 	;
 15458                              <1> 	; (**) ASCIIZ (not UNICODE) long name (max. 128+NUL bytes)
 15459                              <1> 	;
 15460                              <1> 	; Note:
 15461                              <1> 	;	if EDX input is 0
 15462                              <1> 	;		Only File Size will be returned in EAX (*)
 15463                              <1> 	;	if CH > 0 but
 15464                              <1> 	;	   CH & 3Fh is 0, buffer will not used (*)
 15465                              <1> 	;
 15466                              <1> 	; ***********************************************************
 15467                              <1> 	;

 15871                              <1> sysfnf: ; <Find Next File>
 15872                              <1> 	; 25/05/2025
 15873                              <1> 	; 19/05/2025
 15874                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10) ((v2.1.0))
 15875                              <1> 	; 25/08/2024 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9)
 15876                              <1> 	; 29/08/2023 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.6)
 15877                              <1> 	; 08/08/2022
 15878                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
 15879                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016 TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) feature only !
 15880                              <1> 	;           -derived from TRDOS v1.0, INT_21H.ASM-
 15881                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_find_next_file")
 15882                              <1> 	; TRDOS 8086 (v1.0)
 15883                              <1>         ; 	07/08/2011 
 15884                              <1>         ;	Find First File
 15885                              <1> 	;	INPUT:
 15886                              <1>         ;	    none
 15887                              <1> 	;	MSDOS OUTPUT:
 15888                              <1> 	;	    DTA: (Default address: PSP offset 80h)
 15889                              <1> 	;	    Offset  Descrription
 15890                              <1> 	;	    0	    Reserved for use find next file
 15891                              <1> 	;	    21	    Attribute of file found
 15892                              <1> 	;	    22	    Time stamp of file
 15893                              <1> 	;	    24	    Date stamp of file
 15894                              <1> 	;	    26	    File size in bytes
 15895                              <1> 	;	    30	    Filename and extension (zero terminated)
 15896                              <1> 	;	If cf = 1:
 15897                              <1> 	;	    Error Codes: (in AX)
 15898                              <1> 	;	       18 - No more files
 15899                              <1>         ;
 15900                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (v2.0)
 15901                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016
 15902                              <1> 	;
 15903                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
 15904                              <1>        	; 	   none
 15905                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 15906                              <1> 	;	   EAX = 0 if CH input of 'Find First File' > 0
 15907                              <1> 	;	   EAX = First cluster number of file
 15908                              <1> 	;		 if CH input of 'Find First File' = 0
 15909                              <1> 	;	   EDX = File parameters table/structure address
 15910                              <1> 	;
 15911                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
 15912                              <1> 	;
 15913                              <1>  	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
 15914                              <1> 	;
 15915                              <1> 	; Note: If byte [FFF_Valid] = 0
 15916                              <1> 	;	'sysfnf' will return with 'no more files' error.
 15917                              <1> 	;	If byte [FFF_Valid] = 24
 15918                              <1> 	;	'sysfnf' will return with 24 bytes basic parameters
 15919                              <1> 	;	at the address which is in EDX.
 15920                              <1> 	;	If byte [FFF_Valid] = 128
 15921                              <1> 	;	'sysfnf' will return with 128 bytes Find File
 15922                              <1> 	;	Structure/Table at the address which is in EDX.
 15923                              <1> 	;
 15924                              <1> 	; ***********************************************************
 15925                              <1> 	;
 15926                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (Major Modification)
 15927                              <1> 	; ------ TR-DOS 386 v2.0.10 --------
 15928                              <1> 	; FindFile - SysFFF/SysFNF Structure (<=281 bytes):
 15929                              <1> 	;
 15930                              <1> 	; Offset   Parameter			Size
 15931                              <1> 	; ------   ------------------		--------
 15932                              <1> 	; 0	   FindFile_DirEntry		32 bytes (*)
 15933                              <1> 	; 32	   FindFile_Drv			1 byte
 15934                              <1> 	; 33	   FindFile_Directory		65 bytes (104 bytes)
 15935                              <1> 	; 98	   FindFile_Name		13 bytes
 15936                              <1> 	; 111	   FindFile_LongNameEntryLength 1 byte
 15937                              <1> 	; 112	   FindFile_Longname		129 bytes (max.) (**)
 15938                              <1> 	;
 15939                              <1> 	; Parameters table/structure size: max. 280 bytes (**)
 15940                              <1> 	;
 15941                              <1> 	;		; 25/05/2025 (**)
 15942                              <1> 	; Return Options:
 15943                              <1> 	;	CH = 0 -> basic (24 bytes)
 15944                              <1> 	;	CH bits
 15945                              <1> 	;	   bit 0 - FindFile_DirEntry
 15946                              <1> 	;	   bit 1 - FindFile_Drv
 15947                              <1> 	;	   bit 2 - FindFile_Directory (65 bytes)
 15948                              <1> 	;	   bit 3 - FindFile_Name
 15949                              <1> 	;	   bit 4 - FindFile_LongNameEntryLength
 15950                              <1> 	;	   bit 5 - FindFile_Longname (65 bytes) (ASCIIZ)
 15951                              <1> 	;	   bit 6 - use 104 bytes buf for directory
 15952                              <1> 	;	   bit 7 - use 128+1 bytes buf for longname (**)
 15953                              <1> 	; 	examples:
 15954                              <1> 	;	  1Fh -	00011111b needs 112 bytes buffer
 15955                              <1> 	;	  0Fh -	01001111b needs 150 bytes buffer
 15956                              <1> 	;	 0EFh -	11101111b needs 279 bytes buffer
 15957                              <1> 	;	 0FFh -	11111111b needs 280 bytes buffer (**)
 15958                              <1> 	;	 07Fh - 01111111b needs 216 bytes buffer (**)
 15959                              <1> 	;	 03Fh - 00111111b needs 177 bytes buffer (**)
 15960                              <1> 	;
 15961                              <1> 	; (**) ASCIIZ (not UNICODE) long name (max. 128+NUL bytes)
 15962                              <1> 	;
 15963                              <1> 	; Note:
 15964                              <1> 	;	if EDX input is 0
 15965                              <1> 	;		Only File Size will be returned in EAX (*)
 15966                              <1> 	;	if CH > 0 but
 15967                              <1> 	;	   CH & 3Fh is 0, buffer will not used (*)
 15968                              <1> 	;
 15969                              <1> 	; ***********************************************************
 15970                              <1> 	;

 17518                              <1> sysalloc:
 17519                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 17520                              <1> 	; 14/10/2017
 17521                              <1> 	; 20/08/2017 - 01/09/2017
 17522                              <1> 	; 20/02/2017 - 04/03/2017 - 15/05/2017
 17523                              <1> 	; 19/02/2017 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 17524                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
 17525                              <1> 	;
 17526                              <1> 	; Allocate Contiguous Memory Block/Pages (for user)
 17527                              <1> 	; (System call for DMA Buffer allocation etc.)
 17528                              <1> 	;
 17529                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 17530                              <1> 	;	EBX = Virtual address (for user)
 17531                              <1> 	;	     (Physical memory block/aperture
 17532                              <1> 	;	     will be mapped to this virtual address)
 17533                              <1> 	;	ECX = Byte Count
 17534                              <1> 	;	     (will be rounded up to page border)
 17535                              <1> 	;	If ECX = 0
 17536                              <1> 	;	    System call will return with an error (cf=1)
 17537                              <1> 	;	    but ECX will contain maximum size of
 17538                              <1> 	;	    available memory aperture and physical
 17539                              <1> 	;	    (beginning) address of that aperture
 17540                              <1> 	;	    (which have maximum size) will be in EAX.
 17541                              <1> 	;	EDX = Upper limit of the requested physical memory
 17542                              <1> 	;	      block/pages.
 17543                              <1> 	;	     (The last byte address of the memory aperture
 17544                              <1> 	;	      must not be equal to or above this limit.)
 17545                              <1> 	;	If EDX = 0
 17546                              <1> 	; 	   there is NOLIMIT !
 17547                              <1> 	;	If EDX = 0FFFFFFFFh (-1)
 17548                              <1> 	;	   ESI = Lower Limit !
 17549                              <1> 	;		(Beginning of the block must not be 'less'
 17550                              <1> 	;		than this.) (Must be equal to or above...)
 17551                              <1> 	;	   EDI = Upper Limit !
 17552                              <1> 	;		(End of the block must be !less! than this)
 17553                              <1> 	;		(The last byte addr of the memory aperture
 17554                              <1> 	;		must not be equal to or above this limit.)
 17555                              <1> 	;
 17556                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 17557                              <1> 	;	If CF = 0
 17558                              <1> 	;	EAX = Physical address of the allocated memory block
 17559                              <1> 	;	ECX = Allocated bytes (as rounded up to page borders)
 17560                              <1> 	;	EBX = Virtual address (as rounded up)
 17561                              <1> 	;	IF CF = 1
 17562                              <1> 	;	    Requested (size of) Memory block could not be
 17563                              <1> 	;	    allocated to the user!
 17564                              <1> 	;	IF CF = 1 & EAX = 0 (Insufficient memory error!)
 17565                              <1> 	;	   ECX = Total number of free bytes
 17566                              <1> 	;	         (not size of available contiguous bytes!)
 17567                              <1> 	;	If CF = 1 & EAX > 0
 17568                              <1> 	;	   there is not a memory aperture with requested size
 17569                              <1> 	;	   but total free mem is not less than requested size.
 17570                              <1> 	;	   EAX = Physical addr of available memory aperture
 17571                              <1> 	;	   	 with max size 
 17572                              <1> 	;	        (but it doesn't fit to the conditions!)
 17573                              <1> 	;	   ECX = Size of available memory aperture in bytes.
 17574                              <1> 	;	If CF = 1 -> EAX = 0FFFFFFFFh
 17575                              <1> 	;	   Conditions/Parameters are wrong !
 17576                              <1> 	;	   ECX is same with input value.
 17577                              <1> 	;
 17578                              <1> 	; Note:	Previously allocated pages will be deallocated if
 17579                              <1> 	;       new allocation conditions are met.
 17580                              <1> 	;
 17581                              <1> 	; Note: u.break control may be included in future versions
 17582                              <1> 	;
 17583                              <1> 
 17584 00012924 31C0                <1> 	xor	eax, eax ; 0
 17585                              <1> 	; 14/10/2017
 17586 00012926 4A                  <1> 	dec	edx ; is there a limit ?
 17587 00012927 7810                <1> 	js	short sysalloc_1 ;  0 -> 0FFFFFFFFh -> NO LIMIT
 17588 00012929 42                  <1> 	inc	edx ; > 0

 17590                              <1> 	;(round up to page borders)

 17698                              <1> sysdalloc:
 17699                              <1> 	; 19/02/2017 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 17700                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
 17701                              <1> 	;
 17702                              <1> 	; Deallocate Memory Block/Pages (for user)
 17703                              <1> 	; (Complementary call for sysalloc.)
 17704                              <1> 	;
 17705                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 17706                              <1> 	;	EBX = Virtual address (for user)
 17707                              <1> 	;	      (will be rounded up to page border)
 17708                              <1> 	;	ECX = Byte Count
 17709                              <1> 	;	     (will be adjusted to page borders)
 17710                              <1> 	;	If ICX = 0
 17711                              <1> 	;	   nothing to do
 17712                              <1> 	;	If EBX + ECX > User's ESP
 17713                              <1> 	;	   nothing to do
 17714                              <1> 	;
 17715                              <1> 	; Note: u.break control may be included in future versions
 17716                              <1> 	;
 17717                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 17718                              <1> 	;	If CF = 0
 17719                              <1> 	;	   EAX = Deallocated memory bytes
 17720                              <1> 	;	   EBX = Virtual address (as rounded up)
 17721                              <1> 	;	IF CF = 1
 17722                              <1> 	;	   EAX = 0
 17723                              <1> 	;
 17724                              <1> 	; Note:	Main purpose of this call is to deallocate/release
 17725                              <1> 	;	previously allocated (physically) contiguous memory
 17726                              <1> 	;	pages but beginning (virtual) address may not be
 17727                              <1> 	;	followed by physically contiguous pages. So, this
 17728                              <1> 	;	system call will deallocate user's virtually
 17729                              <1> 	;	contiguous memory pages. Also, there is not any
 17730                              <1> 	;	objections to use this system call without sysalloc
 17731                              <1> 	;	system call; only possible objection is to lost data
 17732                              <1> 	;	within user's memory space, if the beginning address
 17733                              <1> 	;	and size is not proper.
 17734                              <1> 	;
 17735                              <1> 	; Note: Empty page tables will not be deallocated!!!
 17736                              <1> 	;       (they will be deallocated at process termination)
 17737                              <1> 	;
 17738                              <1> 	; Note: When the program terminates itself or when it is 
 17739                              <1> 	;	terminated by operating system kernel, all allocated
 17740                              <1> 	;	memory pages will be deallocated during termination
 17741                              <1> 	;	stage. So, 'sysdalloc' is not necessary except 
 17742                              <1> 	;	forgiving memory block to other programs/processes.
 17743                              <1> 	;
 17744 000129DE 8B15[0CB00100]      <1> 	mov	edx, [u.sp]
 17745 000129E4 8B420C              <1> 	mov	eax, [edx+12] ; user's stack pointer
 17746 000129E7 29C8                <1> 	sub	eax, ecx ; esp - byte count
 17747 000129E9 24FC                <1> 	and	al, 0FCh ; dword alignment

 17768                              <1> syscalbac:
 17769                              <1> 	; SYS CALLBACK
 17770                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 17771                              <1> 	; 03/08/2020
 17772                              <1> 	; 16/04/2017
 17773                              <1> 	; 14/04/2017
 17774                              <1> 	; 13/04/2017
 17775                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017
 17776                              <1> 	; 26/02/2017
 17777                              <1> 	; 24/02/2017
 17778                              <1> 	; 21/02/2017 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 17779                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
 17780                              <1> 	;
 17781                              <1> 	; Link or unlink IRQ callback service to/from user (ring 3)
 17782                              <1> 	;
 17783                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 17784                              <1> 	;	BL = IRQ number (Hardware interrupt request number)
 17785                              <1> 	;	     (0 t0 15 but IRQ 0,1,2,6,8,14,15 are prohibited)
 17786                              <1> 	;	     IRQ numbers 3,4,5,7,9,10,11,12,13 are valid
 17787                              <1> 	;	     (numbers >15 are invalid)
 17788                              <1> 	;
 17789                              <1> 	;	BH = 0 = Unlink IRQ (in BL) from user (ring 3) service
 17790                              <1> 	;	     1 = Link IRQ by using Signal Response Byte method
 17791                              <1> 	;	     2 = Link IRQ by using Callback service method
 17792                              <1> 	;	     3 = Link IRQ by using Auto Increment S.R.B. method
 17793                              <1> 	;	    >3 = invalid 
 17794                              <1> 	;
 17795                              <1> 	;	CL = Signal Return/Response Byte value
 17796                              <1> 	;
 17797                              <1> 	;	If BH = 3, kernel will put a counter value  ; 03/08/2020
 17798                              <1> 	;	          (into the S.R.B. addr)
 17799                              <1> 	;		  between 0 to 255. (start value = CL+1)
 17800                              <1> 	;
 17801                              <1> 	;	NOTE: counter value, for example: even and odd numbers
 17802                              <1> 	;	      may be used for -audio- DMA buffer switch
 17803                              <1> 	;	      within double buffer method, etc.
 17804                              <1> 	;
 17805                              <1> 	;	EDX = Signal return (Response) byte address
 17806                              <1> 	;	       		  - or -
 17807                              <1> 	;	      Interrupt/Callback service/routine address
 17808                              <1> 	;
 17809                              <1> 	;	      (virtual address in user's memory space)
 17810                              <1> 	;
 17811                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 17812                              <1> 	;	CF = 0 & EAX = 0 -> Successful setting
 17813                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 & EAX > 0 -> IRQ is prohibited or locked
 17814                              <1> 	;			by another process
 17815                              <1> 	;		 eax = ERR_PERM_DENIED -> prohibited or locked
 17816                              <1> 	;		 eax = ERR_INV_PARAMETER -> 
 17817                              <1> 	;		       invalid parameter/option or bad address
 17818                              <1> 	;
 17819                              <1> 	;	NOTE: Timer callbacks are set by using 'systimer'
 17820                              <1> 	;	      system call (IRQ 0, PIT and IRQ 8, RTC)
 17821                              <1> 	;
 17822                              <1> 	;	      Direct keyboard access is performed by using
 17823                              <1> 	;	      Keyboard Interrupt (INT 32h)
 17824                              <1> 	;
 17825                              <1> 	;	      It is prohibited here because:
 17826                              <1> 	;		1) Signal Response Byte method has not advantage
 17827                              <1> 	;		   against INT 32h, function AH = 1. Also,
 17828                              <1> 	;		   keyboard service interrupt will return with
 17829                              <1> 	;		   ascii and scan codes (AL, AH) while
 17830                              <1> 	;		   SRB method has only 1 byte space for ascii code
 17831                              <1> 	;		   or scan code. One byte signal response is used
 17832                              <1> 	;		   for ensuring very simple and very fast
 17833                              <1> 	;		   virtual to physical memory address conversion
 17834                              <1> 	;		   without any memory page crossover risk.
 17835                              <1> 	;		   (Otherwise double page conversion or word
 17836                              <1> 	;		   alignment would be needed.)
 17837                              <1> 	;		2) Badly written user code (callback code)
 17838                              <1> 	;		   can prevent keyboard and timesharing functions
 17839                              <1> 	;		   of the operating system via continuous and long
 17840                              <1> 	;		   keyboard event handling by callback service.
 17841                              <1> 	;		   (It can cause to lose immediate keystroke
 17842                              <1> 	;		   response from hardware to user.)
 17843                              <1> 	;		3) If user will check any keyboard events, 'getkey'
 17844                              <1> 	;		   (or 'getchar') must have more priority than other
 17845                              <1> 	;		   (video etc.) events because only control ability
 17846                              <1> 	;		   on a procedural infinite loop is a keyboard or
 17847                              <1> 	;		   mouse event. So user can use keyboard function
 17848                              <1> 	;		   at the end or at the beginning of a loop.
 17849                              <1> 	;		   In this case, INT 32h is used for that purpose
 17850                              <1> 	;		   and timer interrupt etc. callbacks can be used
 17851                              <1> 	;		   for dynamic and synchronized data refresh/transfer
 17852                              <1> 	;		   while cpu is in a static loop (without polling).
 17853                              <1> 	;		   Keyboard Int callback is not more useful because
 17854                              <1> 	;		   already a manual check (a key is pressed or not)
 17855                              <1> 	;		   can be performed (via INT 32h, AH = 1) efficiently
 17856                              <1> 	;		   in a loop to prevent a locked infinitive loop.
 17857                              <1> 	;
 17858                              <1> 	;	    Disk IRQs (6,14,15) have been phohibited from ring 3
 17859                              <1> 	;	    callback because, disk operations (file system services
 17860                              <1> 	;	    etc.) are independent from user program, for fast disk r/w.
 17861                              <1> 	;	    They are not more useful at ring 3 while they are in use
 17862                              <1> 	;	    by standard diskio functions which are mandatory part of
 17863                              <1> 	;	    (monolithic) OS kernel and mainprog command interpreter.
 17864                              <1> 	;	    INT 33h diskio functions are enough for user level disk
 17865                              <1> 	;	    r/w.
 17866                              <1> 	;
 17867                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 - IRQ CALLBACK structures (parameters):
 17868                              <1> 	;
 17869                              <1> 	;	   [u.irqlock] = 1 word, IRQ flags (0-15) that indicates
 17870                              <1> 	;			which IRQs are locked by (that) user.
 17871                              <1> 	;		        Lock and unlock (by user) will change
 17872                              <1> 	;			these flags or 'terminate process' (sysexit)
 17873                              <1> 	;			will clear these flags and unlock those IRQs.
 17874                              <1> 	;
 17875                              <1> 	;		   	Bit 0 is for IRQ 0 and Bit 15 is for IRQ 15
 17876                              <1> 	;
 17877                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).owner	 : 1 byte, user, [u.uno], 0 = free (unlocked)
 17878                              <1> 	;
 17879                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).method : 1 byte for callback method & status
 17880                              <1> 	;			   0 = Signal Response Byte method
 17881                              <1> 	;			   1 = Callback service method
 17882                              <1> 	;			   >1 = invalid for current 'syscalback'.
 17883                              <1> 	;			or(+) 80h = IRQ is in use by system (ring 0)
 17884                              <1> 	;			            function (audio etc.) or
 17885                              <1> 	;			   	    a device driver.
 17886                              <1> 	;			(system function will ignore the lock/owner)
 17887                              <1> 	;
 17888                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).srb	: 1 byte, Signal Return/Response byte value
 17889                              <1> 	;			  (a fixed value by user or a counter value
 17890                              <1> 	;			 from 0 to 255, which is increased by every
 17891                              <1> 	;			 interrupt just before putting it into
 17892                              <1> 	;			 the Signal Response byte address
 17893                              <1> 	;			 (This is not used in callback serv method)
 17894                              <1> 	;
 17895                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).addr	: 1 dword
 17896                              <1> 	;			  Signal Response Byte address (physical)
 17897                              <1> 	;			  		-or-
 17898                              <1> 	;			  Callback service address (virtual)
 17899                              <1> 	;
 17900                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).dev	: 1 byte
 17901                              <1> 	;			  0 = Default device or kernel function
 17902                              <1> 	;			  		-or-
 17903                              <1> 	;			  1-255 = Assigned device driver number
 17904                              <1> 	;
 17905                              <1> 	;	   (x) = 3,4,5,7,9,10,11,12,13
 17906                              <1> 	;
 17907                              <1> 	;
 17908                              <1> 	;	NOTE: If user's process/program calls the kernel (INT 40h)
 17909                              <1> 	;	      while it is already running in a (ring 3) callback
 17910                              <1> 	;	      service, kernel will force (convert) system call to
 17911                              <1> 	;	      'sysrele' (sys release). So, this feature provides
 17912                              <1> 	;	      easy and simple usage of callback services without
 17913                              <1> 	;	      falling into deepless <please 'callback me' then
 17914                              <1> 	;	      let me 'callback you'> cycles! (User must return
 17915                              <1> 	;	      from callback service by using 'sysrele' system
 17916                              <1> 	;	      call, without a significant delay. Otherwise user
 17917                              <1> 	;	      process/program may be late to catch the next event
 17918                              <1> 	;	      within same callback purpose.
 17919                              <1> 	;
 17920                              <1>

 18186                              <1> syschdir: ; Change Current (Working) Drive & Directory (for user)
 18187                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0
 18188                              <1> 	; 12/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.11
 18189                              <1> 	;	Erdogan Tan & Google AI Collaborator
 18190                              <1> 	;	Explicit CHDIR Re-validation	
 18191                              <1> 	;
 18192                              <1> 	; 30/12/2017 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0) 
 18193                              <1> 	;
 18194                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
 18195                              <1>         ;          EBX = Directory name (ASCIIZ string) address
 18196                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 18197                              <1> 	;          cf = 0 -> eax = 0
 18198                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
 18199                              <1> 	;
 18200                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
 18201                              <1> 	;
 18202                              <1> 	; NOTE: If drive name is not included, only the working
 18203                              <1> 	; directory (for user, not for drive/OS) will be chanded.
 18204                              <1> 	; If there is a drive name (as A:, B:, C:, D: etc.)
 18205                              <1> 	; at the beginning of the ASCIIZ (directory) string,
 18206                              <1> 	; working drive and working directory (for user) 
 18207                              <1> 	; will be changed together.
 18208                              <1> 	; (When the program is terminated, MainProg -internal
 18209                              <1> 	; shell- will reset working directory to the previous
 18210                              <1> 	; -current- logical drive's current directory again.)
 18211                              <1> 
 18212 00012B53 89DE                <1> 	mov	esi, ebx
 18213                              <1> 	; file name is not forced, change directory as temporary
 18214 00012B55 31C0                <1> 	xor	eax, eax
 18215                              <1> 	;mov	[FFF_Valid], ah ; 0 ; reset
 18216                              <1> 	;call	set_working_path

 18239                              <1> syschmod: ; Get & Change File (or Directory) Attributes
 18240                              <1> 	; 02/01/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10 (v2.1)
 18241                              <1> 	; 22/09/2025
 18242                              <1> 	; 26/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
 18243                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 18244                              <1> 	; 19/01/2021
 18245                              <1> 	; 30/12/2017 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 18246                              <1> 	;
 18247                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
 18248                              <1>         ;          EBX = File/Directory (ASCIIZ) name address
 18249                              <1> 	;	    CL = New attributes (if CL < 40h)
 18250                              <1> 	;	    CL >= 40h -> Get File Attributes
 18251                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 18252                              <1> 	;          cf = 0 -> EAX = File attributes (in AL)
 18253                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
 18254                              <1> 	;
 18255                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
 18256                              <1> 	;
 18257                              <1> 	; MSDOS File Attributes:    (bit value of attrib byte)
 18258                              <1> 	;	ATTR_READ_ONLY	=	01h  (bit 0, 'R')
 18259                              <1> 	;	ATTR_HIDDEN	=	02h  (bit 1, 'H')
 18260                              <1> 	;	ATTR_SYSTEM	=	04h  (bit 2, 'S')
 18261                              <1> 	;	ATTR_VOLUME_ID	=	08h  (bit 3)
 18262                              <1> 	;	ATTR_DIRECTORY	=	10h  (bit 4)
 18263                              <1> 	;	ATTR_ARCHIVE	=	20h  (bit 5, 'A')
 18264                              <1> 	;	ATTR_LONG_NAME	=	ATTR_READONLY |
 18265                              <1> 	;				ATTR_HIDDEN |
 18266                              <1> 	;				ATTR_SYSTEM |
 18267                              <1> 	;				ATTR_VOLUME_ID
 18268                              <1> 	;	The upper two bits of attributes must be 0.
 18269                              <1> 
 18270                              <1> 	; Note:	* If ATTR_DIRECTORY is set, only directory names
 18271                              <1> 	;	  will be searched (and S,H,R,A attributeds of
 18272                              <1> 	;	  the directory will be changed.)
 18273                              <1> 	;	* If ATTR_VOLUME_ID is set, 'syschmod' system call
 18274                              <1> 	;	  will return with 'permission denied' error.
 18275                              <1> 	;	* If ATTR_DIRECTORY is not set, only file names
 18276                              <1> 	;	  will be searched (and S,H,R,A attributes of the
 18277                              <1> 	;	  file will be changed.)
 18278                              <1> 	;
 18279                              <1> 	; (Ony Super User can change S,H,R attributes.)
 18280                              <1>

 18579                              <1> systime: ; Get System Date&Time
 18580                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0
 18581                              <1> 	; 16/05/2026
 18582                              <1> 	; 15/05/2026
 18583                              <1> 	; 03/05/2026
 18584                              <1> 	; 01/05/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.11
 18585                              <1> 	; 30/12/2017 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 18586                              <1> 	;
 18587                              <1>         ; INPUT -> BL =
 18588                              <1> 	;	    0 = Get Date&Time in Unix/Epoch format
 18589                              <1> 	;	    1 = Get Time in MSDOS format
 18590                              <1> 	;	    2 = Get Date in MSDOS format (1980->1980)
 18591                              <1> 	;	    3 = Get Date&Time in MSDOS format (1980->1980)
 18592                              <1> 	;	01/05/2026
 18593                              <1> 	;	    4 = Get/Return System Timer Ticks (18.2 Hz)
 18594                              <1> 	;		Note: If the system timer frequency is 100 Hz
 18595                              <1> 	;	             (18.2 Hz for the current kernel version),
 18596                              <1> 	; 		     the carry flag will be set on return.
 18597                              <1> 	;		-However, even if the system is running at 100 Hz,
 18598                              <1> 	;		 the number of ticks converted to 18.2 Hz will
 18599                              <1>         ;		 be returned-
 18600                              <1> 	;		100Hz to 18.2Hz conversion: int(timerticks*182/1000)
 18601                              <1> 	;	    5 = Get/Return System Timer Ticks (100 Hz)
 18602                              <1> 	;		Note: carry flag will be set at return
 18603                              <1> 	;		      if system timer frequency is NOT 100 Hz
 18604                              <1> 	;		(it is 18.2 Hz for current kernel version)
 18605                              <1> 	;		-However, even if the system is running at 18.2 Hz,
 18606                              <1> 	;		 the number of ticks converted to 100 Hz will
 18607                              <1>         ;		 be returned-
 18608                              <1> 	;		18.2Hz to 100Hz conversion: int(timerticks*1000/182)
 18609                              <1> 	;	    6 = Get Date&Time in MSDOS packed (direntry) format
 18610                              <1> 	;		(1980->0)
 18611                              <1> 	;	16/05/2026
 18612                              <1> 	;	    7 = Get Timer Ticks OVERFLOW Status
 18613                              <1> 	; 	    8 = Get Day Of The Week
 18614                              <1> 	;
 18615                              <1> 	;	    9 & other values (>9) =
 18616                              <1> 	;		System timer ticks will be returned
 18617                              <1> 	;		in EAX and Carry Flag will be set.
 18618                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 18619                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 3
 18620                              <1> 	;          EAX = Current Time (RTC)
 18621                              <1> 	;		AL = Second (DL in MSDOS)
 18622                              <1> 	;		AH = Minute (CL in MSDOS)
 18623                              <1> 	;	   	HW of EAX = Hour (CH in MSDOS)
 18624                              <1> 	;	   EDX = Current System Date (RTC)
 18625                              <1> 	;		DL = Day (DL in MSDOS)
 18626                              <1> 	;		DH = Month (DH in MSDOS)
 18627                              <1> 	;		HW of EDX = Year (CX in MSDOS)
 18628                              <1> 	;
 18629                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 2
 18630                              <1> 	;	   EAX = Current System Date (RTC)
 18631                              <1> 	;		AL = Day (DL in MSDOS)
 18632                              <1> 	;		AH = Month (DH in MSDOS)
 18633                              <1> 	;		HW of EAX = Year (CX in MSDOS)
 18634                              <1> 	;
 18635                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 1
 18636                              <1> 	;          EAX = Current Time (RTC)
 18637                              <1> 	;		AL = Second (DL in MSDOS)
 18638                              <1> 	;		AH = Minute (CL in MSDOS)
 18639                              <1> 	;	   	HW of EAX = Hour (CH in MSDOS)
 18640                              <1> 	;
 18641                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 0
 18642                              <1> 	;          EAX = Unix (Epoch) Time Ticks/Seconds
 18643                              <1> 	;
 18644                              <1> 	;	01/05/2026
 18645                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 4
 18646                              <1> 	;	   EAX = System timer tick count (18.2 Hz)
 18647                              <1> 	;	   if CF = 1 -> system is running at 100 Hz
 18648                              <1> 	;	      and tick count is converted to 18.2 Hz
 18649                              <1> 	;	      Conversion: int(timerticks*182/1000)
 18650                              <1> 	;	   0 = midnight, 00:00:00:00
 18651                              <1> 	;          if CF = 0 -> system timer is running at 18.2 Hz
 18652                              <1> 	;	      and tick count is actual on the system side
 18653                              <1> 	;
 18654                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 5
 18655                              <1> 	;	   EAX = System timer tick count (100 Hz)
 18656                              <1> 	;	   if CF = 1 -> system is running at 18.2 Hz
 18657                              <1> 	;	      and tick count is converted to 100 Hz
 18658                              <1> 	;	      Conversion: int(timerticks*1000/182)
 18659                              <1> 	;	   0 = midnight, 00:00:00:00
 18660                              <1> 	;          if CF = 0 -> system timer is running at 100 Hz
 18661                              <1> 	;	      and tick count is actual on the system side
 18662                              <1> 	;
 18663                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 6
 18664                              <1> 	;	   EAX = Date&Time in MSDOS/direntry (packed) format
 18665                              <1> 	;		AX (time) bits = hhhhhmmmmmmsssss
 18666                              <1> 	;			bits 0-4: seconds divided by 2, 0-28
 18667                              <1> 	;			bits 5-10: minute (0-59)
 18668                              <1> 	;			bits 11-15: hour (0-23)
 18669                              <1> 	;		HW of EAX (date) bits = yyyyyyymmmmddddd
 18670                              <1> 	;			bit 0-4: day of the month (1-31)
 18671                              <1> 	;			bit 5-8: Month (1-12)
 18672                              <1> 	;			bit 9-15: Year (0-127) [Year-1980]
 18673                              <1> 	;	16/05/2026
 18674                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 7
 18675                              <1> 	;	    EAX = Timer OVERFLOW ([TIMER_OFL]) Status
 18676                              <1> 	;	        = 1 -> overflow occurred
 18677                              <1> 	;               = 0 -> no overflow occurred
 18678                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 8

 18680                              <1> 	;	    NOTE: Each time the RTC date is updated/written,
 18681                              <1> 	;		  ("RTC_55:" in 'timer.s')
 18682                              <1> 	;	          the dow value in CMOS_DAY_WEEK will
 18683                              <1> 	;		  be reset/invalidated
 18684                              <1> 	;	    if CF = 1 or EAX = 0 -> error (invalid)
 18685                              <1> 	;
 18686                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 9 (or BL input > 9)
 18687                              <1> 	;	    CF = 1 (always.. for current kernel version)
 18688                              <1> 	;	    EAX = System timer ticks (no error code!)
 18689                              <1> 	;
 18690                              <1> 	;

 18692                              <1> 	;		 (at the return of system call)

 18830                              <1> sysstime: ; Set System Date&Time
 18831                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0
 18832                              <1> 	; 21/05/2026
 18833                              <1> 	; 17/05/2026
 18834                              <1> 	; 16/05/2026
 18835                              <1> 	; 15/05/2026
 18836                              <1> 	; 14/05/2026
 18837                              <1> 	; 12/05/2026
 18838                              <1> 	; 03/05/2026
 18839                              <1> 	; 01/05/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.11
 18840                              <1> 	; 31/12/2017
 18841                              <1> 	; 30/12/2017 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 18842                              <1> 	;
 18843                              <1> 	; INPUT -> BL =
 18844                              <1> 	;	    0 = Set Date&Time in Unix/Epoch format
 18845                              <1> 	;	    1 = Set Time in MSDOS format
 18846                              <1> 	;	    2 = Set Date in MSDOS format
 18847                              <1> 	;	    3 = Set Date&Time in MSDOS format
 18848                              <1> 	;	    4 = Set System Timer (Ticks) - 18.2 Hz -
 18849                              <1> 	;	    5 = Convert/Save current time to/as
 18850                              <1> 	;		18.2 Hz system timer ticks
 18851                              <1> 	;	    6 = Convert MSDOS Date&Time to UNIX format
 18852                              <1> 	;		without setting system date&time ; (test)
 18853                              <1> 	;	    7 = Convert UNIX Date&Time to MSDOS format
 18854                              <1> 	;		without setting system date&time ; (test)
 18855                              <1> 	;	01/05/2026
 18856                              <1> 	;	    8 = Convert packed MSDOS Date&Time to UNIX format
 18857                              <1> 	;		without setting system date&time ; (test)
 18858                              <1> 	;		ECX = packed MSDOS date&time
 18859                              <1> 	;		ECX (time) bits = hhhhhmmmmmmsssss
 18860                              <1> 	;			bits 0-4: seconds divided by 2, 0-28
 18861                              <1> 	;			bits 5-10: minute (0-59)
 18862                              <1> 	;			bits 11-15: hour (0-23)
 18863                              <1> 	;		HW of ECX (date) bits = yyyyyyymmmmddddd
 18864                              <1> 	;			bit 0-4: day of the month (1-31)
 18865                              <1> 	;			bit 5-8: Month (1-12)
 18866                              <1> 	;			bit 9-15: Year (0-127) [Year-1980]
 18867                              <1> 	;	    9 = Convert UNIX Date&Time to packed MSDOS format
 18868                              <1> 	;		without setting system date&time ; (test)
 18869                              <1> 	;		ECX = Unix Epoch Time
 18870                              <1> 	;	   10 = Set System Timer (Ticks) - 100 Hz input -
 18871                              <1> 	;		((conversion: input*182/1000))
 18872                              <1> 	;	16/05/2026
 18873                              <1> 	;	   11 = Set Day Of The Week
 18874                              <1> 	;		ECX = day of the week (to be set)
 18875                              <1> 	;		    = 1 -> sunday
 18876                              <1> 	;		    = 7 -> saturday
 18877                              <1> 	;
 18878                              <1> 	;	   12-0FFh = invalid !
 18879                              <1> 	;
 18880                              <1> 	;	  ECX = Time (or Timer) value in selected format
 18881                              <1> 	;	  EDX = Date value in MSDOS format if BL=2,3,6
 18882                              <1> 	;
 18883                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 18884                              <1> 	;	If CF = 0 -> (if BL input < 11 --> CF = 0)
 18885                              <1> 	;	   For BL input = 0,1,2,3,4,5,10
 18886                              <1> 	;			-> EAX = tick count (18.2 Hz)
 18887                              <1> 	;	   For BL input = 6,8 -> EAX = unix epoch time
 18888                              <1> 	;	   For BL input = 7 -> EAX = Time, EDX = Date
 18889                              <1> 	;			AL = second (0-29)
 18890                              <1> 	;			AH = minute (0-59)
 18891                              <1> 	;		 HW of EAX = hour (0-23)
 18892                              <1> 	;			DL = day (1-31)
 18893                              <1> 	;			DH = month (1-12)
 18894                              <1> 	;		 HW of EDX = year (any, 16 bit)
 18895                              <1> 	;	   For BL input = 9 -> EAX = packed date&time
 18896                              <1> 	;			AX = msdos/direntry time (packed)
 18897                              <1> 	;		 HW of EAX = msdos/direntry date (packed)
 18898                              <1> 	;	   16/05/2026
 18899                              <1> 	;	   For BL input = 11
 18900                              <1> 	;		 EAX = day of the week (in AL)
 18901                              <1> 	;		     = ECX input (CL)
 18902                              <1> 	;	       if CF = 1 -> EAX = 0
 18903                              <1> 	;			   (invalid set value or error)
 18904                              <1> 	;
 18905                              <1> 	;	If CF = 1 -> (invalid BL input, >= 12)
 18906                              <1> 	;	   EAX = ticks count [TIMER_LH] ; 18.2 Hz
 18907                              <1> 	;
 18908                              <1>

 19576                              <1> 	; Get/Set Environment Variables
 19577                              <1> 	;
 19578                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022

    16                              <1> ; DIR.ASM (c) 2004-2011 Erdogan TAN  [07/01/2004] Last Update: 09/10/2011
    17                              <1> 
    18                              <1> set_run_sequence:
    19                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
    20                              <1> 	; 23/12/2016
    21                              <1> 	; 10/06/2016
    22                              <1> 	; 22/05/2016
    23                              <1> 	; 20/05/2016
    24                              <1> 	; 19/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
    25                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 feature only !
    26                              <1> 	;
    27                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
    28                              <1> 	;	AL = process number (next process)
    29                              <1> 	;
    30                              <1> 	;	this process must be added to run sequence
    31                              <1> 	;
    32                              <1> 	;	[u.pri] = priority of present process
    33                              <1> 	;
    34                              <1> 	;	DL = priority (queue)
    35                              <1> 	;	     0 = background (low) ; run on background
    36                              <1> 	;	     1 = regular (normal) ; run as regular
    37                              <1> 	;	     2 = event (high)     ; run for event
    38                              <1> 	;
    39                              <1> 	;	1) If the requested process is already running:
    40                              <1> 	;	   a) If present priority is high ([u.pri]=2)
    41                              <1> 	;	      and requested priority is also high,
    42                              <1> 	;	      there is nothing to do! Because it has been
    43                              <1> 	;	      done already (before this attempt).
    44                              <1> 	;	   b) If present priority is high ([u.pri]=2)
    45                              <1> 	;	      and requested priority is not high, there is
    46                              <1> 	;	      nothing to do! Because, it's current
    47                              <1> 	;	      run queue is unspecified, here. (It may be in
    48                              <1> 	;	      a waiting list or in a run queue; if the new
    49                              <1> 	;	      priority would be used to add it to relavant
    50                              <1>         ;             run queue, this would be wrong, unnecessary
    51                              <1> 	;	      and destabilizing duplication!)
    52                              <1> 	;	   c) If present priority is not high ([u.pri]<2)
    53                              <1>         ;             and requested priority is high (event),
    54                              <1> 	;	      process will be added to present priority's
    55                              <1> 	;	      run queue and then, priority will be changed
    56                              <1> 	;	      to high ([u.pri]=2).
    57                              <1> 	;	   d) If present priority is not high ([u.pri]<2)
    58                              <1> 	;	      and requested priority is not high, [u.pri]
    59                              <1> 	;	      value will be changed. There is nothing to do
    60                              <1> 	;	      in addition. (The new priority value will be
    61                              <1> 	;	      used by 'tswap/tswitch' procedure at 'sysret'
    62                              <1> 	;	      or 'sysrele' stage.)
    63                              <1> 	;
    64                              <1> 	;	2) If the requested process is not running:
    65                              <1> 	;	   a) If requested priority of the requested
    66                              <1> 	;	      (next) process is high (event) and priority
    67                              <1> 	;	      of present process is not high, the requested
    68                              <1> 	;	      process will be added to ('runq_event') high
    69                              <1> 	;	      priority run queue and then present (running)
    70                              <1> 	;	      process will be stopped (swapped/switched out)
    71                              <1> 	;	      immediately if it is in user mode, or it's
    72                              <1> 	;	      [u.quant] value will be reset to 0 and (then)
    73                              <1> 	;	      it will be stopped at 'sysret' stage.
    74                              <1> 	;	   b) If requested priority of the requested
    75                              <1> 	;	      (next) process is high (event) and priority
    76                              <1> 	;	      of present process is also high, the requested
    77                              <1> 	;	      process will be added to ('runq_event') high
    78                              <1> 	;	      priority run queue and present (running)
    79                              <1> 	;	      process will be allowed to run until it's
    80                              <1> 	;	      time quantum will be elapsed ([u.quant]=0).
    81                              <1> 	;	   c) If requested priority of the requested
    82                              <1> 	;	      (next) process is not high ('run for event'),
    83                              <1> 	;	      there is nothing to do. Because, it's current
    84                              <1> 	;	      run queue is unspecified, here. (It may be in
    85                              <1> 	;	      a waiting list or in a run queue; if the new
    86                              <1> 	;	      priority would be used to add it to relavant
    87                              <1>         ;             run queue, this would be wrong, unnecessary
    88                              <1> 	;	      and destabilizing duplication!)
    89                              <1> 	;
    90                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
    91                              <1> 	;	none
    92                              <1> 	;
    93                              <1> 	;	[u.pri] = priority of present process
    94                              <1> 	;
    95                              <1> 	;	cf = 1, if the request could not be fulfilled.
    96                              <1> 	;
    97                              <1> 	;	NOTE:
    98                              <1>         ;          * Processes in 'run as regular' queue can run
    99                              <1> 	;	     if there is no process in 'run for event' queue
   100                              <1> 	;	     ('run for event' processes have higher priority)
   101                              <1> 	;	   * When [u.quant] time quantum of a process is
   102                              <1> 	;	     elapsed, it's high priority ('run for event')
   103                              <1> 	;	     status will be disabled, it can be run in sequence
   104                              <1> 	;	     of it's actual run queue.
   105                              <1> 	;	   * A 'run on background' process will always be
   106                              <1> 	;	     sequenced in 'run on background' (low priority)
   107                              <1> 	;	     queue, it can run only when other priority queues
   108                              <1> 	;	     are empty. (idle time processes, e.g. printing)
   109                              <1> 	;
   110                              <1> 	; Modified registers: eax, ebx, edx
   111                              <1> 	;
   112                              <1>

   582                              <1> sp_init:
   583                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
   584                              <1> 	; 07/11/2015
   585                              <1> 	; 29/10/2015
   586                              <1> 	; 26/10/2015
   587                              <1> 	; 23/10/2015
   588                              <1> 	; 29/06/2015
   589                              <1> 	; 14/03/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - 115200 baud)
   590                              <1> 	; 28/07/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1 - 9600 baud)
   591                              <1> 	; Initialization of Serial Port Communication Parameters
   592                              <1> 	; (COM1 base port address = 3F8h, COM1 Interrupt = IRQ 4)
   593                              <1> 	; (COM2 base port address = 2F8h, COM1 Interrupt = IRQ 3)
   594                              <1> 	;
   595                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EAX, ECX, EDX, EBX))
   596                              <1> 	;
   597                              <1> 	; INPUT:  (29/06/2015)
   598                              <1> 	;	AL = 0 for COM1
   599                              <1> 	;	     1 for COM2
   600                              <1> 	;	AH = Communication parameters
   601                              <1> 	;
   602                              <1> 	;  (*) Communication parameters (except BAUD RATE):
   603                              <1> 	;	Bit	4	3	2	1	0
   604                              <1> 	;		-PARITY--   STOP BIT  -WORD LENGTH-
   605                              <1> 	;  this one -->	00 = none    0 = 1 bit  11 = 8 bits
   606                              <1> 	;		01 = odd     1 = 2 bits	10 = 7 bits
   607                              <1> 	;		11 = even
   608                              <1> 	;  Baud rate setting bits: (29/06/2015)
   609                              <1> 	;		Retro UNIX 386 v1 feature only !
   610                              <1> 	;	Bit	7    6    5  | Baud rate
   611                              <1> 	;		------------------------
   612                              <1> 	;	value	0    0    0  | Default (Divisor = 1)
   613                              <1> 	;		0    0    1  | 9600 (12)
   614                              <1> 	;		0    1    0  | 19200 (6)
   615                              <1> 	;		0    1	  1  | 38400 (3)
   616                              <1> 	;		1    0	  0  | 14400 (8)
   617                              <1> 	;		1    0	  1  | 28800 (4)
   618                              <1> 	;		1    1    0  | 57600 (2)
   619                              <1> 	;		1    1    1  | 115200 (1)
   620                              <1> 
   621                              <1> 	; References:
   622                              <1> 	; (1) IBM PC-XT Model 286 BIOS Source Code
   623                              <1> 	;     RS232.ASM --- 10/06/1985 COMMUNICATIONS BIOS (RS232)
   624                              <1> 	; (2) Award BIOS 1999 - ATORGS.ASM
   625                              <1> 	; (3) http://wiki.osdev.org/Serial_Ports
   626                              <1> 	;
   627                              <1> 	; Set communication parameters for COM1 (= 03h)
   628                              <1> 	;

   702                              <1> sp_i3:

   720                              <1> 					; 6 = 19200 baud

   725                              <1> 					; of the divisor value

   733                              <1> 	JMP	$+2			; I/O DELAY

   762                              <1> sp_setp: ; Set serial port communication parameters
   763                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)

   782                              <1> 	;	Bit	4	3	2	1	0
   783                              <1> 	;		-PARITY--   STOP BIT  -WORD LENGTH-
   784                              <1> 	;  this one -->	00 = none    0 = 1 bit  11 = 8 bits
   785                              <1> 	;		01 = odd     1 = 2 bits	10 = 7 bits
   786                              <1> 	;		11 = even

   790                              <1> 	;		------------------------

   792                              <1> 	;		0    0    1  | 9600 (12)
   793                              <1> 	;		0    1    0  | 19200 (6)
   794                              <1> 	;		0    1	  1  | 38400 (3)
   795                              <1> 	;		1    0	  0  | 14400 (8)
   796                              <1> 	;		1    0	  1  | 28800 (4)

   799                              <1> 	;
   800                              <1> 	; (COM1 base port address = 3F8h, COM1 Interrupt = IRQ 4)
   801                              <1> 	; (COM2 base port address = 2F8h, COM1 Interrupt = IRQ 3)
   802                              <1> 	;
   803                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EAX, ECX, EDX, EBX))
   804                              <1> 	;

   811                              <1> 	inc	ebx ; COM2 control byte offset
   812                              <1> sp_setp1:

   818                              <1> 	mov	al, [ecx+b_div_tbl]

   821                              <1> 	mov	cx, ax ; CL = Line status, CH = Modem status
   822                              <1> 	test	al, 80h
   823                              <1> 	jz	short sp_setp2

   825                              <1> stp_dnr_err:

   827                              <1> 	; CL = Line status, CH = Modem status
   828                              <1> 	stc

   830                              <1> sp_setp2:

   932                              <1> 	; 27/01/2011 - 08/02/2011

   934                              <1> 	; depending on command tail
   935                              <1> 	; (procedure is derivated from CMD_INTR.ASM
   936                              <1> 	; file or dir locating code of internal commands)
   937                              <1> 	; (This procedure is prepared for INT 21H file/dir
   938                              <1> 	; functions and also to get compact code for
   939                              <1> 	; internal mainprog -command interpreter- commands)
   940                              <1> 	;
   941                              <1> 	; INPUT: DS:SI -> Command tail (ASCIIZ string)
   942                              <1> 	; AL = 0 -> any, AL > 0 -> file name is forced
   943                              <1> 	; AH = CD -> Change directory permanently
   944                              <1> 	; AH <> CD -> Change directory as temporary
   945                              <1> 	;
   946                              <1> 	; OUTPUT: ES=DS, FindFile structure has been set
   947                              <1> 	;        RUN_CDRV points previous current drive
   948                              <1> 	;        DS:SI = FindFile structure address

   950                              <1> 	;        AX, BX, CX, DX, DI will be changed

   952                              <1> 	;        stc & AX = 0 -> Bad command or path name
   953                              <1> 	; -----------------------------------------------
   954                              <1> 	;
   955                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (05/10/2016)

   957                              <1> 	;	ESI = File/Directory Path (ASCIIZ string)

   960                              <1> 	;       AL > 0 -> file name is forced
   961                              <1> 	;       AH = CD -> change directory as permanent
   962                              <1> 	;       AH <> CD -> change directory as temporary
   963                              <1> 	;
   964                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
   965                              <1> 	;	FindFile structure has been set
   966                              <1> 	;       RUN_CDRV points previous current drive
   967                              <1> 	;       ESI = FindFile_Name address ; 12/10/2016
   968                              <1> 	;
   969                              <1> 	;       cf = 1 -> Error code in EAX (AL)

  1637                              <1> set_IRQ_callback_addr:
  1638                              <1> 	;
  1639                              <1> 	; This routine sets return address
  1640                              <1> 	; to start of user's interrupt
  1641                              <1> 	; service (callback) address
  1642                              <1> 	;
  1643                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  1644                              <1> 	;	EDX = callback routine/service address
  1645                              <1> 	;	      (virtual, not physical address!)
  1646                              <1> 	;	[u.sp] = kernel stack, points to
  1647                              <1> 	;		 user's EIP,CS,EFLAGS,ESP,SS
  1648                              <1> 	;		 registers.
  1649                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  1650                              <1> 	;	EIP (user) = callback (service) address
  1651                              <1> 	;	CS (user) = UCODE
  1652                              <1> 	;	EFLAGS (user) = flags before callback
  1653                              <1> 	;       ESP (user) = ESP-4 (user, before callback)
  1654                              <1> 	;	[ESP](user) = EIP (user) before callback
  1655                              <1> 	;
  1656                              <1> 	; Note: If CPU was in user mode while entering
  1657                              <1> 	;	the timer interrupt service routine,
  1658                              <1> 	;	'IRET' will get return to callback routine
  1659                              <1> 	;	immediately. If CPU was in system/kernel mode
  1660                              <1> 	;	'iret' will get return to system call and
  1661                              <1> 	;	then, callback routine will be return address
  1662                              <1> 	;	from system call. (User's callback/service code
  1663                              <1> 	;	will be able to return to normal return address
  1664                              <1> 	;	via a 'sysrele' system call at the end.)
  1665                              <1> 	;
  1666                              <1> 	; Note: User's IRQ callback service code must be ended
  1667                              <1> 	;	with a 'sysrele' system call !
  1668                              <1> 	;
  1669                              <1> 	;	For example:
  1670                              <1> 	;
  1671                              <1> 	;	audio_IRQ_callback:
  1672                              <1> 	;	    ...
  1673                              <1> 	;	    <load DMA buffer with audio data>
  1674                              <1> 	;	    ...
  1675                              <1> 	;	    mov eax, 39 ; 'sysrele'
  1676                              <1> 	;	    int 40h ; TRDOS 386 system call (interrupt)
  1677                              <1> 	;
  1678                              <1> 
  1679                              <1> 	;mov	edx, [edx+IRQ.addr] ; Callback service address
  1680                              <1> 	;			    ; (Virtual address)
  1681                              <1> 
  1682 00013998 8B2D[0CB00100]      <1> 	mov	ebp, [u.sp]; kernel's stack, points to EIP (user)
  1683 0001399E 895500              <1> 	mov	[ebp], edx
